title: Ben Johnson on Bears' late-game confidence | Press Conference
text: The team went out and found a way to win.  Well, in several areas we weren't at our best, and yet, finding a way to win was the most important thing.  So, uh, it was a big, big win in that sense.  Well, several players stood out. Uh, I already talked about Jaylon Johnson's interception for a touchdown.  That was a key play in the game. Uh, I thought Devin Bush played one of his best games as a Chicago Bear, uh, which was great to watch. Hey, Awesome Booker made some great plays for us.  Eh, their intensity , their effort, they keep improving week after week.  And so a lot of guys there on the defensive side played some really good football for us, which we needed. Uh, I know the lads are excited to have a little break this week, to rest their bodies, to take their minds off football for a minute before we get to the final stretch of the season.  So, I'll open up the space from here.   We'll start with Jason Lieser. Go ahead, Jason. Hey Ben, what are the lessons you 're emphasizing with Caleb so he can use a game like that to grow ? Well, yeah, I think when you look at the four interceptions, uh, there were a couple where we didn't see the coverage as well as we would have liked, and there are a couple where we tried, uh, to avoid disaster , and, uh, we didn't exactly, uh, do what we needed to do with the ball in terms of discarding it and living for the next play. So, uh, hey, I know he was trying to throw away or get rid of a couple of those, and we just need to do a better job of accomplishing that. And, you know, the others are just the coverage recognition part .  That's what Todd Bowles' defense is known for, and they can make it challenging.  And so, uh , these will be good lessons to put in our memory bank and take advantage of, uh, the next time we face a team like this. Were you able to clarify with him that it wasn't just a departure from how he had been playing in general, but a very abrupt change from how he started that match? Yes, no, I don't necessarily know if it was just one thing.  Uh, I think there were a lot of factors that came into play there. Well, you know, we had a lot of penalties that contributed to that. Um, and there was a lot that happened in that game.  Um, we lost our rhythm as an offense. Um, as the one in charge of the plays, I have to do a better job to get us back on track. Uh, and once again, I give a lot of credit to that defense.  It's a good unit and, uh , they make it very challenging.  And in a way, we started the game well and finished it strongly. Uh, but that middle, that second and third quarter, wasn't exactly our style of play.  So um, we'll pick up from there. Let's go with Dan Weder.  Go ahead, Dan. Ben, the 38-yard pass to Colton on the game- winning field goal drive was obviously a broken coverage, but how do you feel you pressured the Buccaneers to cause that coverage to fail, whether it was through timing, movement, or anything else that triggered it? Yes, um, I don't know if it can necessarily be predicted, but um, you know, we all know that movements and changes cause communication problems. Um, but it's a matter of luck whether you actually get a meltdown like that. So we have some good, solid plays. We try to take into account all the problems they present in terms of protection, and the quarterback reads the play, and if someone isn't where they should be, he makes them pay.  So, uh, Caleb did a great job on that particular play. You said this morning that you were going to think a little about performance.  What is your process for finding the healthy point to reflect on that performance and ensure it is productive? Well, the good news is that all our lads, as grateful as we are to win, and at the end of the day , that's the ultimate goal we're aiming for . But there's a certain standard we want to reach every week, and I think good teams, even when they get wins, if they don't reach those benchmarks, they fall short. And uh, I felt that from our group, which is a good thing.  I think that's the next evolution of this team.   It's not just about winning, but the way we play.  So, we have to continue like this. Hey, you know, we have some time now. I think we have a great opportunity to analyze these first nine games and see what we're doing well and what we can build on for the final stretch of the season, and of course, some areas for improvement where we need to make progress. So it will be an interesting analysis over the next few days as a coaching staff to make sure we are properly aligned to improve. Go ahead, Kevin Fishbain.  Go ahead, Kevin. Hi, Ben. Obviously, these are different teams and situations , but a couple of years ago when Jared had that five- interception game in Houston and you guys came away with the win, what can be learned from that experience when analyzing this game? Yes, I don't like either of those two parties.   Looking back on it, I think it's really indicative of the whole team when you can overcome something like that. And you know, in a 17- game season, there will be games where not everyone is at their best and we need others to help us compensate. And that was the case yesterday.  As a unit, the offensive did not perform exactly as we are capable of doing. I think there are several players who would say it wasn't their best game, certainly not this year. And yet, as a team, other teammates were able to fill the void and we kept saying that we just had to find a way to score one more point than the opponent, and we did it. So, you know, the defense is really the unsung hero of this game. I'm sure you guys are giving them the credit they deserve out there , but to get five turnovers and then the blocked punt and only allow 10 points, that's a truly phenomenal job and it's a mentality .   You know, they go out onto the field and they know every time they step onto the grass that their objective is to not allow the opponent to score points, and they did that at a high level yesterday. Go ahead, Courtney Cronin. more Ben. Quick, sorry to keep going on the offensive, but with Theo, in that six-day span from Seattle, where he plays every play against that team and then battles through injury earlier in the week and manages to play every play last night .  What did you appreciate about what he/she has shown you during the last week? Yes, I think it's tremendous growth, and certainly for him, being a young player, to understand that this team still needs him. We're talking about games during the season where you won't be at 100%, and we still need you to go out there and give every ounce of effort at 90% or 85%. And I think that was the case with him last night , putting in the effort and being there for his teammates. I think that's present in this entire team right now.  You see a guy like Tyreek Stevenson fall for a moment. You see a guy like Kyler Gordon go down for a minute and they're fighting. They're dying to get back on the field to finish the game with their teammates, so I'm very proud of the team in terms of their willingness to go out and compete and finish these matches. Go ahead, Courtney. Ben, as you do your self-assessment this week, where will you start with your ground game to try and find more consistency coming out of the end of the schedule? Yes, well, I think we're going to analyze what we're doing right now .  This makes us more consistent and, schematically, I think we are a little different from where we were this year compared to last year.  You know, there are some things after last year's bye week that we were able to build on, and hopefully we can find details like those in areas where we can really make it more consistent, as you said. I think that, over the course of nine games, there have only been three of those nine where we averaged more than 4 yards per carry, which, simply on our terms, is not enough at this point.  And those boys know it.  Particularly as the climate continues to shift into a bear climate, we will need to rely more on that ground game, and it's going to have to answer for us. Well, I need to analyze whether it's the fact that we're not making as many explosive plays in the ground game right now Is that why the average is low, or are we simply not moving the line of slugging? What are those factors?  So having a sample of nine games at this point will be very good for us to analyze. And with those five games without Kyle, do you feel that will provide an answer as to what that offensive combination has been missing these past few weeks? Yes, I mean, Kyle is a big part of that ground game and I think he's proven his worth over the last year and a half.  So, like I said last week, when we can get him back on the field, he'll make us a better team and certainly a better running game. We continue with Pat Finley.  Go ahead, Pat. Ben, you're in a slightly unusual situation, as you're on break week and you're going to do a self-assessment, but there's also the deadline for changes tomorrow.  What will the next 22 and a half hours be like in terms of trying to determine what can be fixed with the players they have and with the concepts, versus whether they might need reinforcements? Yes, I think Ryan is doing a phenomenal job every day.  He is analyzing and seeing how we can improve this squad, what we need most. The coordinators are undoubtedly talking every day about where their concerns lie within the team. So we'll see.  We'll see if we need to make another move or two, or if we'll stay as we are. I feel very confident with the guys we have in this locker room right now ;  I think they have shown by now that we can find a way to win every week with this group. Let's go with the last two, Phil and Dan. Go ahead, Phil. Thank you. Ben, on both of Caleb's central interceptions, it appears that the protection failed in different ways. What did you see, and is that a problem with some of the defensive pressure you 've seen in recent games, where they 're pressing especially through the middle? No, we need to block better.  Those were pressures we were prepared for before the game, so we need to block better. Then Kyler Gordon said that you guys probably needed a pinch on the ass, meaning, you know, an ugly win like this to give you a wake-up call, I guess that's what he meant. What do you think about it? Yes, I like the fact that we won. I believe there are things we can learn from every victory and every defeat. Our process doesn't really change. Last question, Dan. Ben, you said last night, excuse me, that the final series was as comfortable as you felt all night calling the plays.   There seemed to be a universal feeling that everyone felt the work was going to be finished. What did you feel about yourself and the group in a game like that, a tied game, and just having the feeling that you would be able to pull it off? Yes, I think it's unique because we haven't been in that situation much this year, and I hate to keep dwelling on last year. But maybe it's that confidence that many of those familiar faces are still part of this team, that we're going to be at our best when the pressure is greatest, and it just felt like we were back on the bike, and we were riding it again, you know?  It's hard to describe, to be honest, but I'm glad they felt the same way I did, because it wasn't like we had much say on the sidelines.  It wasn't necessary.  It was just a matter of moving forward.  We kept fighting and, you know , a great play finally came along and those guys pulled it off. So it was very well done by the entire offensive team at that time. Very good.  Thank you, coach.

title: Quarterback Michael Penix Jr. reflects on international matchup vs. Bengals | Press Conference
text: Yes, we're just beating ourselves up , you know, too many penalties.  You know, we emphasize that a lot every single day during the week.  You know, the coach always shows in team meetings how many penalties we had in the previous practice and it's usually less than one or two per day. We had a couple of clean days too, but whenever we go out here and have 12 penalties between the three units, it's difficult to win like that.  So yeah, that's what I'm saying, you know, whenever you're in those situations you have to take advantage of every opportunity we have. So whenever we get a penalty like that, taking us from yard one to yard 15 or whatever, that's devastating, and we can't do that.  You know, great football teams don't do that.  You can't beat us, we can't defeat ourselves.  We have to go out there and we have to beat the other team. Yes, definitely.  I mean, we always felt like we were in the game, so for us we always knew we were just one offensive series away.  We knew the defense was going to get a save for us. So we just had to go out and execute, and we didn't do it consistently enough;  We achieved it in that series you mentioned, but we have to find ways to do it consistently, and we didn't do it today.   I mean , we're all professionals . We understand what happened out there today. We beat ourselves in many areas of the game and it's difficult, so talking with the team it's like we have to correct those things. Just let the guys know that we need to fix those things, and, you know, it's nothing the guys don't already know. We went into the locker room after the game and we know what happened on that pitch, and we knew that wasn't who we wanted to be this season. And we have to prove it if we want to win American football games. Yes, after the Benz, it's the best stadium.   It 's incredible.  It was a beautiful stadium. Yes, it was incredible to be able to play there.  It's a beautiful, beautiful, beautiful stadium. Say it again. What has it been like being here? Oh, it's been, it's been incredible, you know, for us, to play the sport we love, to be able to go to different countries and, you know, to have all the fans coming to see what we love to do It's fantastic to be able to expand our sport, the one we love so much, on a global level.  And it's a blessing to be able to do it .   I told the lads before the game not to take this opportunity lightly.   Being able to travel the world doing what we love is a blessing, so I told them not to take it for granted. Yes, obviously we're going to correct the things we need to correct from today.   We're going to review the video and clean up a lot of things.  We have a lot to improve if we want to win American football games .  But once we do that, we'll be totally focused on the Chiefs. We know a good team is coming to the Benz , but we have to play our own game and if we do, we'll love the results. Yes, I just want to thank all the fans who came and made this trip.  The fans from Madrid, from Spain, coming and filling the stadium, it was incredible. It was a fantastic experience for all of us;  Obviously we wanted to win, but it was still an amazing experience. Yes, I felt good in there.  Every time I found an opening, I could run and get a couple of first downs.   I'm often told that I don't usually run, but today I felt that it was what we needed in those situations, so I took advantage of it. Very well, thank you all.

But in the second one, you know, I was just paying homage to Miles.  You know, we have the same name, so I thought, damn, with a two-capture game, I'm going to do Miles' celebration. And then in that second one, it felt like, you know, it seemed like you showed a blitz and then they, whatever, didn't immediately pull it out. Um, were you surprised that they didn't see you coming and that you were able to escape in that second capture? Yes, I honestly thought they were going to block me on that play. But I thought they were going to block me once I, uh, broke the formation. Okay, I think those are all the questions we have for you, Miles.

I you >> How happy with with penalties having been an issue, how pleased were you >> Yeah, we had the three, I guess, on special teams, right? And then but the offense and defense stayed clean. Um and that's been that's been hurting us the last couple games. So, you've got to you got to make sure you you you focus in on that, and then let's learn from it. Let's keep that going. Gives you a chance when you're not going backwards on offense and giving them forward progress on defense, it's hard enough to neutralize an offense or defense in this league anyways without the penalty. So, you Um as long as we can keep that going, that's great. >> Thanks, coach. >> All right, good. Thank you. >> What felt like it was going on there? >> Yeah, I mean, >> if I'm able to play, I'm I'm going to play. All right, that's part of the game and it's part of playing, you know, it it scares you in moments when you get some pains in in in certain areas of your body, and so uh obviously I didn't feel great. Um but was able to kind of get it worked on a little bit, especially at halftime, um and then I was able to go out there and and play the rest of the game. >> Did it like I mean, did you immediately feel like a question at all about coming back in, or how do you like that? >> Yeah, I mean, you just never know, you know, I mean, obviously I had the knee injury last year. You never know what's going to be the the the final um result or outcome of of an injury. Um but at the same time, you just try to let the doctors and trainers do their work, and so um definitely um something that scare scares you more than I think than anything, but uh we were able to get back there and and give it a go. >> How do you feel now? >> Uh, I feel good now. I mean, obviously get the win and um the adrenaline's pumping. I'm sure I'll be sore tomorrow, um, but um we'll we'll get right to it, you know, we'll get to work on it. We'll get ourselves ready to go and um it's great to get the win now and now it's about getting ourselves ready for next week. No, I I I know I I needed to. No, but he he did that at Texas Tech a lot, so I got drafted second overall. So, uh I saw it a lot on TV. I I don't like being the guy that's getting hit. Um, so I'll try to stay away from that. Yeah, I think guys just did a great job doing their assignments, you know, a lot of times the assignments are where it comes down to in the trenches and um guys were physical. They did their assignments well and they were able to get themselves into the end zone and so that's glad to see cuz you want that going throughout the year and so it was a step in the right direction. Um, yeah, I know the first one um we were trying to look for a man-type coverage and we got I think it was cover four but played like man underneath and uh we were able to run guys across the field. Had miscommunication on how they were passing off in zone and so giving giving Kenneth a a pass and then uh getting him to the end zone. Um, and then the other one was the uh the screen. Great screen call by coach Reed. I mean, the offensive line getting out there and they scored the touchdowns which you want on screens. Um, and so it was just a great great call at the right time. Um, and then the the one that Trev was past, man, I'm but I I'm not mad, but it was Yeah, he's getting better and better at it. I mean, he has the talent and he can catch the football. And so it's just about giving him more opportunities to to go out there and show that. And so we've done that this year. He's shown that he can do it. Um, and he did he had a great game in multiple ways. I mean, running the football, catching the football, blocking, doing what it takes to be a great running back in this league and uh we'll keep doing that as we go forward. Yeah, I mean, you want to be a team that that likes each other cuz at the end of day it comes down to are you willing to lay it all on the line? I mean, a lot a lot of times we talk about the offense and us scoring touchdowns and and doing all this type of stuff, but it's the offensive line. It's how it goes. And they don't get the glory. They don't get the the kind of the be standing up here on the podium and doing all different type of stuff. But they're they're who make us go, and they're the engine of the offense, same with the defensive line and and everything like that. And so, you want to have a team that's that's close, that really likes each other and then loves being out there on the field and playing, and they kind of give it all. And that comes with stuff that you do off the field as much as you do on it. >> We had the game we saw Xavier go off for the appears to be a left hamstring injury. You've had injuries with Tyreek Hill and Mecole Hardman with his own hamstring. Just how difficult is it to sort of build that confidence, that chemistry when you build a team having a lot of receiver injuries throughout >> Yeah, I mean, it's part of it, but at the same time, I mean, you you want to have those guys out there. And I had a had a he was having a good game today. Um made some tough physical catches, kind of especially down there at the goal line. And so, we'll we'll we'll hopefully it's not as bad as it looked out there. Um I haven't got to talk to him or the trainers or anything like that, but it's kind of that next man guy I mean, next next man up mentality. And we've had guys that have gotten reps because of the injuries. And so, um they'll have to step in and make the plays happen um whenever their number's called. >> We've seen you pretty active on social media before. Um but you know, you've got the trade deadline coming up. Are you going to be monitoring to see if there's any rumors out there about a wide new wide receiver coming in there? >> I I I'll leave that all up to Veach and Coach Reid. Um I just when I whoever's in that building, I go out there and try to make and try to make the most of it and win football games. And I think we've done a great job of that with a lot of different uh guys. And um I see the work these guys put in every single day. And and they're they're ready. They're ready to go out there and make plays when their number's called. And so, uh I'll leave that up to those guys. >> Patrick, when you guys went into the half, there was such games that had a lot of time of possession. How did you guys flip that script and dominate the second half? >> Yeah, I mean, it started with that first drive, you know, both sides of the ball. I mean, offensively we were able to get down there, have a good drive, score a touchdown. And then defensively get a stop, you know. And and a lot of times when you you get that momentum, especially coming out of halftime, after you've made adjustments, you can kind of ride that through the rest of the game. And so, um we were able to do that, and so they had they they played really well. They had a lot of great drives. They controlled possession uh a lot um in that first half, and I thought that first drive was important to get get points and kind of get the possession back in our favor. >> We're going to go across here. Let's go to Sam. >> Yeah, I mean that we have confidence in him. I mean that's that's pretty much it, man. I've seen him make field goals at the biggest stages that you can make in this league, and so um I want him to know that I have as much confidence in him as I ever had, and so uh just trying to give him that that vote of confidence there at that moment um and kind of keep it moving. >> All right. Back to you, Mark. >> What did the team say to you about the elbow injury you returned to do or elbow area? >> Well, I haven't I haven't got that yet. So, we're going to go do some testing here whenever whenever I get done at at this media stuff right here, and um we'll get a better understanding of it, and I'm sure Coach Arians will give you an update tomorrow. >> And did you feel limited? I mean, you were dealing with some limitation. >> I felt like out of half I wasn't throwing the ball the way I wanted to, but as the game went on and we kind of continued to work through it and kind of got warmed back up, I thought I kind of started throwing the ball better um towards the end of the second half. Um and so that'll be important this week is kind of getting that the swelling and the fluid out of it so I can be ready to go from the first snap next week. >> And to ask about to that, like before last year when you got hurt, it seemed like you always were just right away back in. Did it feel different when you got hurt this time like uh playing stuff like that? >> It didn't It didn't feel different, but anytime it's elbows and knees, it's always scary just cuz you just don't know. You know what I mean? Like even my knee last year uh after we were doing the initial test, I thought I could walk off the field. I thought I was going to be good, and then all of a sudden you do one test, and you're just out. And that kind of that that stuff scares you. Um so I think that was more than anything. I felt like I I could once I could throw the football from the stories you hear whenever you can grab the ball and try to throw it, you can't throw. And so once I threw the football, I knew it wasn't it wasn't um hopefully I mean I haven't done the test yet. I wouldn't ligament type stuff. It was more muscle type stuff, and so that'll be important to kind of get worked out this week. >> Last two times in the eight years you've been here, a couple of things. I mean, when you pitched, did you ever have the elbow issues at all? >> No, my I I didn't even ice when I when I used to pitch, so that probably wasn't good for me, but uh uh yeah, no, I never had any elbow issues. Uh thank God, knock on wood. Um but um uh hopefully we can stay away from those. >> And finally, this farce of short-yardage stuff, I mean, there's been lots of talk on social media. Fans have been going about sneaks and all that. And you guys have said that you guys ran the sneak >> What was your view of the play? What's what's it been like in practice this last couple weeks to try to find the right way to get those short yards? >> Yeah, I mean, we've had that in practice these last few weeks. Um we kind of got we kind of got messed up with the timing of it. We were trying to surprise the defense when we broke the huddle. And then with the spot, and we had to re-huddle again, and their defense kind of got to adjust to it. Um so, obviously losing the element of surprise, but we got to do it. We got to we got to make it happen, and you got to work on that stuff. You got to work on sneak sneaks and stuff like that. And so, it's new to the guys, but uh as long as we keep executing at a high level short yardage-wise, uh we'll find different ways to do it. >> Last one, Nate. You know that Travis has been working through that ankle injury. >> Mhm. >> So, but you guys have you guys have a full record for most yards between a pass and a catcher and a and a quarterback from tight ends. Just what's it been like to watch Travis sort of navigate through this season and have the success he had today as you >> No, I mean, he he he does a he does a great job, man. He he's as tough as tough as you you you'll get in this league. And he'll fight through anything to go out there and play, and he he's he's he's so damn accountable to himself and his teammates that he he won't let anything hold him hold him back. And so, um it's always great to have him on the field cuz he's going to make plays happen. He'll fight through every injury, every everything um in order to help this team um and I think that's uh the guys you want on your on your team whenever you are competing for a championship. >> Thanks, Patrick. Congratulations. >> Oh, man, it's a testament to all my teammates, you know, um one person get the credit, but it takes a village. It takes a lot of unselfish teammates for me to be successful, and especially getting 90 sacks. It it's not an easy task, but it takes a lot of unselfish unselfish individuals. So, super grateful for the teammates on this journey of 11 year journey that I've had in order for me to even get close to >> Chris, we talked about it earlier. His pads are up. Well, um I said it earlier, man. We got 10 games left. Well, nine after today. And a sack a game is what? 10 sacks. So, I I think we kind of put put too much emphasis on getting sacks. I mean, they eventually come. And then when they come, they come in spurts like today. Um I think most importantly it's about um being detailed, playing physical, and more so on defense setting the tone. >> What do you think allowed several of you to get home today? >> Just being relentless. Um being relentless. Um playing tight man coverage on the back end. I think um the coverage and the sacks kind of go hand in hand. When they have good coverage on the back end, it allows us time to get there. And I think they went hand in hand today and allowed us to get back there a couple times. >> You were on your second sack. It came from the edge. You haven't had many sacks this year on that side. Did you have to advocate for yourself to to rush from that end? Or what led to that sort of sack happening from that specific spot? >> It's just Fangio moving me around. Um he realizes I'm getting a lot of slides in the inside. So, in order for me to kind of get a one-on-one, he kind of has to move me around. And I got to utilize my opportunities on the edge. >> And actually he wants you to You want to do that more often? Is that something that you think you guys can be successful with? >> For For me, it's about whatever gives us a advantage to get a one-on-one or to get the opportunity to rush the passer. I don't really care where I'm at. Long as I'm getting the opportunity to rush the passer. >> Chris, Chris, you know that you and Justin George got the same kind of pressures too in the holes in the second half. Just what did you see in how they performed? >> Well, listen. We're feeding off of each other. The momentum, uh energy, I think uh I'm a big believer that energy is contagious. And we're playing off of one another. And um we're enjoying the game, enjoying to see each other having success. And I think there's something we can continue to build off of going into Atlanta. Um to another tough environment. And more so just to get back on track as a team. >> Chris, when when Patrick got hurt you jumped up and kind of held him up. You know, what was going through your mind when you saw that hit and then how hurt he looked and then >> Yeah, 15 is important to this team, man. Just got to make sure 15 is okay. And more so he was limping off the field, so I just want to make sure my quarterback is good. >> Were you surprised he was right back in there? >> No, Pat is a warrior. >> The Jets have had some struggles in the red area this year. You guys kept them out of the end zone for field goals. What goes into that, keeping them out of the end zone? >> I think being detailed. We got to have great coaches who put us in position to know what's coming, especially in the red zone. And being detailed as players to and when you know what's coming is your job is a little easier. So, we've been so far we've been really, really good in the red zone. You know, we go back to last week we kept them out of the red They scored two on us out of five tries, but you know, we can something we can still build off of. Emphasizing on keeping them out of the red zone, saving four points on the board. >> Chris, the guy you passed today, Tamba Hali, what's your relationship like with him? What did he mean to you when you were a young defensive lineman coming out of Arkansas? >> You know, I when I came here I had Tamba, Justin, a lot of guys who had a lot of success on this team before me I was able to sit on the bench and watch these guys and watch them prepare, watch what they eat, how they how they prepare throughout the week. And I was able to learn a lot from them those guys. I actually still talk to Tamba. My son plays on his 707 team. We're still very close. So, to to pass him, you know, and with all the work and sacrifice he made for this organization means a lot. >> Chris, you've been in this league a long time, man. How important is it to keep that positive attitude and things like that? >> I think um it's only two things you can control in life. It's your attitude and your effort. And I I try to stay with a positive attitude no matter the circumstances. Cuz, you know, at times we we the football season goes through like this. At times you can get low on yourself. It is never really as bad as you think. It's never really as good as it seems. So, you know, stay positive. Um stay in even keel. Never too high, you never too low. And the storm will eventually pass. >> You have the title of CEO of Sack Nation. Does that game like today mean Sack Nation more? >> Listen, I know uh last week I was like sacks don't matter. I lied. Sacks are everything. >> [laughter] >> Oh, sorry. She wants me up here all day. Okay. She wants me here. >> One other thing about Patrick, you referred to him as a warrior at the time you're doing your stuff on your side of the ball, but does that have actual ripples, you know, across the team and even on game day to know your quarterback is wired that way? >> I mean, I I think it's motivational. I mean, if we want to go back to um when Pat actually had the knee injury and like 3 days later he was in the indoor throwing the ball. You know, just speaks volumes of mentally where he's at and how competitive he is. Uh I think you know, as teammates it's like if he can do this, why are we not doing this? Or why are we not playing through this? You know what I mean? So, I definitely think it's a ripple effect and shows the character of the team. >> Last week, Chris, you had a chance to close out the game in the fourth quarter and got away. Today in the third quarter, you had >> minus nine yards to the Jets. What was the difference today that kind of had that killer instinct kicking in? >> Uh I think it was just detail on all areas of football. Though, I mean, the back end was playing really really good coverage on their wide outs. Uh it wasn't just me getting there. It was Ashton. It was George. I think everyone was racing towards the quarterback and when everyone is operating on one accord, uh it is easier for us to get off the field. When things start getting out of whack, we're not playing as detailed as we're coached, then you start to see the flaws that happen. So, we eliminated a a of penalties today also. Um we did have one off side our Mason. They were we Those are penalties we can fix, you know what I mean? So, other than that, um, we did okay today. >> Thank you everybody. >> Thank you. >> Hey Chris, I'm going to let you go. Yes, you've you've been great both in the receiving receptions and you've been great catching balls here and being on both sides. Can you talk about how the team around you helps you get your offense going today? >> Yeah, first off I'll start with coaches. You know, they see I can catch the ball and run the ball. You know, they put the ball in my hands. Um, secondly like the O-line, tight ends, wide receivers do a great job of, um, making my job a lot easier to go out there and make those plays. >> And then you guys went down trailing in possession of the ball time wise by a lot. What was the you know, half time adjustments to come back and pull back in the second half? >> Yeah, honestly in the first half, you know, we was making a lot of mistakes. Um, and you know, you you make a lot of mistakes then you'll be losing, but um, you know, when we went to half time we straightened up everything and got the details right and started to come out and execute. >> Chris, can you just walk us through that screen play, you know, your second touchdown? Just what you see on that. >> Yeah, yeah. Um, yeah, came out. Uh, Pat dumped it to me. I was open. You know, the O-line, I seen them in front of me, so really just followed those guys and hit outside and you know, it was wide open. >> What's it been like being such a major part of the passing game this year in Seattle? Didn't do a ton of that last year. >> Yeah, obviously it feels good to make plays either way, you know, running the ball or catching the ball, but definitely catching the ball cuz, you know, I've been able to catch the ball since I was younger and you know, being able to coach sees that and putting the ball in my hands that way means a lot to me. >> You're about halfway through the season here. Like you were talking about, you're more involved in the passing game. You also have a career high in touchdowns already with 11 now. Is this what you were hoping for when you signed with K-State? >> Yeah, definitely. You always want to, you know, get opportunities to, you know, make plays or make a positive impact on the team, so definitely means a lot to me. >> Chris, on that that play you're talking about, the screen play, when you're in the huddle and you hear it called, are you like, this is the perfect call? Or is it right when you catch it and turn around? When do you When do you know that this is going to be >> Yeah, I got to say when you catch it and then turn around cuz sometimes on screens it it don't go This is just football in general. It don't go the way you expect it to, so but yeah, definitely once you catch it and turn around and you see the O line in front of you and you know not too many defenders in front of you. >> How many guys do you think he took out along the >> I don't know. I just put my head in his back and went, you know. I'm sure he took out a lot of guys and you know the guys around was blacking us well, so it was a it made it much easier for me to make that play. >> Can I ask you about the sequence of Tagovailoa getting hurt? What did you see? What did you think >> Yeah, I know I seen him you know get sacked or whatever hit get his arm hit, but I'm not sure. I didn't really think too much into that, you know. I'm just glad he was able to finish the game with us. >> What do you think about the fact that he didn't miss a play after >> That's just type of mentality he has, you know, that's the type of competitor he is and you know a great leader of the team on and off the field and he'll continue to continue to be that way. >> Did you feel kind of some responsibility for after Tua went down to say, you know, I got this. I can take over here. >> Yeah, definitely I always want to, you know, when my number's called make plays, but you know, at the end of the day it's a It takes everybody, you know, and I know I'm not the only one out there, so everybody got another touchdown and Jaylen even got the game winning touchdown. Talk to us a little bit about your room and how much those young guys mean to you. >> Yeah, they mean a lot to me, you know. They like my younger brothers, you feel me, so definitely love to see them go out there and shine, you know, and his touchdown, you know, we already knew he was going to go out there dance, you know, cuz he always love to dance and that's just the energy he bringing. Being able to see Iggy go out there and make some plays as well, it meant a lot to me and you know, we're going to watch it and you know, probably laugh about it when we get to the room. >> It's kind of like a lot like like basketball or you're talking about when a guy has a hot hand and you got to keep feeding him and let him shoot. Do you you feel that way when you when you in game it's like, man, I'm hot. You can just just keep feeding me. >> Yeah, definitely. I feel like that goes for everybody. If you you're in a rhythm, you want to stay in that rhythm, so uh think that giving the ball to the hot hand is, you know, really important in sports. >> You guys closed out this game on a 21-nothing run. What does that say about your team? >> Um you know, that's just the whole team, it takes all all takes the special teams, offense, and defense, you know. Uh the defense played a great game as well. Um and you know, it takes all of us. >> Last one, Cam. >> Like I was saying, you know, half the season now with the guys what's it been like to get to know Travis as a teammate and just see what he does on the field from your vantage point? >> Yeah, it's been great. You know, he's a vocal leader and uh on and off the field, like I said about uh Pat. You know, he brings the energy every day. Um as practice, as games, you know, he the same person. He know he cares about us off the field as well, so it's been great to build that relationship and just relationships uh all around the >> Thanks, Cam. >> Yep.

Um, I think when we you eliminate some of the the penalties that we've had that have set us back and you you look at it, I think you're um you're playing pretty good football. Um, uh, before we hit that twoame stretch there where we had the losses, we were right at the top of, you know, most of the offenses in the league and [clears throat] we're still up there halfway decent. So, that's uh you know, we're in good position. But, uh my if if you're one of my guys, I'm telling you that you can see when you get rid of those those negative plays, uh good things can happen. It's hard to stop a run game, it's hard to stop a pass game, and a blend of of that with the screens and all that stuff. It it can be tough to stop at times. So, you just can't go backwards. Let's go next to Sam. Go ahead, Sam. >> Hey, Andy. Um, it looked like on on on the film that Chris uh Jones had his most effective day. Wonder if you saw it the same and and if so, what what do you feel like brings out his best in days like that? >> Yeah. So, well, first of all, you got he got some singled he got singled up a few times and so you know, you're playing us that and I thought schematically the guys did a great job getting him in that spot and moving him around. Uh not that they we've we've tried to do that in the past, but they've kind of followed him and uh with a back or a tight end or motioning somebody in position to to chip him with a tight end. So, um, listen, he he was able to single up and and took advantage of it. And, uh, when he's one-on-one, it's a he's a hard one to stop. >> And then also just in the run game specifically, wonder if you could just comment on what you thought of your offensive line and their uh the their job in in the run game. >> Yeah, I thought I thought we were strong uh for the most part. Um, there's some things obviously we can work on, but I would kind of the same thing that I mentioned about the Dline and working on some of the fundamental things. I think the [clears throat] the things that we had asked the offensive line to work on, I thought they took that to heart and and really really uh helped clean up a couple things there. Uh, the fact that we didn't have any penalties helped us. That was that was one of the big things, but also fundamentally just some of the things getting off the ball and and um putting more pressure maybe on the defensive front. >> Let's go next to Todd Lebo. >> Hey coach, just a a a couple little quick things, just housekeeping stuff. Any update on Josh Simmons and how his rehab is going? Um, yeah, he's doing good. >> And as I was watching the the play yesterday, I had binoculars when Patrick was down there hurt and it looked like EB was getting after Emit pretty good on that play. Was he supposed to give a chip to David Bailey or I mean, is that just one of those kind of young guy pass things? Um, just what was what was the deal with that part of >> Yeah. Yeah. Anytime you know there's that much penetration, yeah, you give a little chip to them. Yeah. But listen, it's the tackles responsibility to block them. That's that's primary thing. So the chip is just icing on the cake. >> Exactly. [clears throat] Um and as far as like penalties go, when you guys go back and look at the film, you have a day where you have really clean. Did you play all that much cleaner or is it just kind of the eb and flow of the league? Sometimes they call some things and sometimes they don't. You know what I'm saying? Or is it does it always did it really feel like everything was a whole lot cleaner than other games or just sometimes they don't call penalties? In the eyes of the officials, we played more clean. >> Gotcha. Thanks, coach. >> All right, >> let's go next to Todd Palmer. >> Hey, coach. Um, I just wondered if you could speak to or offer any insight into what conversations you have with Brett uh with the trade deadline tomorrow. Obviously, Taekquin out for an extended period of time. Rashid's already missed some time. Now it's possible. Xavier, well, how comfortable are you with the depth and the young guys there and their ability to step up and and perform or or are you guys having conversations about reinforcing that position? >> Yeah, I thought, you know, I tell you, Royals, I thought did a nice job about the young guys. I thought he did a a nice job and uh Sai were were kind of working in just as an update on our own guys. We feel pretty good about him on on some things there. So, in his improvement, um although his production, he didn't have much production yesterday as far as catches and all that go. But, um as you know, Todd Brett always keeps his eyes open. I don't have to say anything. Um but he he's always looking and trying to improve the roster and so uh that part hasn't changed. Um he's out there, uh uh searching. So, and doing his due diligence, right? So, uh with his guys. Yeah. >> Okay, we've got two left. Go ahead, Mac. >> I'm not getting him right now. >> You should be able to unmute now, man. >> Oh, hey. Hey, coach. Can you hear me? >> I can hear you now. >> Hey, sorry about that. Um, so watching the game back, I mean it looks like I mean you've mentioned Creed Humphrey's play. It's it's the run, the blocking, the pass blocking, it's all there. It just feels like maybe a snap a game or so is just a little off. Do you think that's a mechanical issue or are you seeing something maybe mental? What what's your what's your take on that? >> Yeah, so um yes, I mean I've assume there's all of the above. He's working on that and um that's not like him. So he's he's cleaning all that up. We'll get that straight. >> Okay, >> Nate Taylor, go ahead and close us out. >> So Andy, just a quick question on Patrick. Do you anticipate that his reps or his week will be slightly different just because of trying to get some of that swelling out of the right elbow or is it too early to tell uh how his practice is going to go this week? >> Yeah, give me a couple days on that. I mean, just till we we have to get out there and and [clears throat] do it. And we'll see where see where he's at. I He's feeling Listen, he feels pretty good today. We we'll we'll see where where it goes. He's sore, but >> um I'm glad we're not practicing today. >> Thank you, coach. We're all done.

title: Reactions to Fernando Mendoza Being Named QB1 as Kirk Cousins Is Traded to Vikings
text: [music] >> Welcome to Raiders Weekly. I'm JT along with Paul Gutierrez who joins us from Raiders.com this week. An exciting times as a trade went down. Fernando Mendoza will be the starter as Kirk Cousins gets traded for a third round pick to Minnesota. How did you see it? >> Yeah, I saw it JT. Thanks for having me in and really the way I look at it is this is just kind of an an extension, a continuation of the plan that was put in place when John Spytek and and Clint Kubiak joined forces during the off season and they drafted uh um Fernando Mendoza. They they signed Kirk Cousins and it was literally in the press conference we just came from. Uh John Spytek said look the plan was this all along that Kirk Cousins was going to play until something changed. Something changed. The trade deadline came to fruition. Fernando Mendoza is ready to go. We're starting the Fernando Mendoza era now. >> First off outstanding job by Kirk Cousins as the quarterback for this team. He had the team out to a three and 0 start. They were four and four. They were competitive. He was a total pro. Mark Davis said once a Raider always a Raider. He will always be welcome back Paul in this building and the fact that he mentored Fernando Mendoza and we really haven't seen Fernando yet as a starter. We don't know how long those dividends will pay off but everyone's excited in the building. >> Absolutely and it's like what I was saying earlier is that this was the plan from the beginning. I remember sitting right next to Clint Kubiak at the owners meetings in March in Arizona and he said look in a perfect world a rookie quarterback doesn't play right away. He sits and learns at the knee of a veteran and this was before they drafted uh Fernando. This is before they even signed uh uh Kirk to come in and and do what he did. so this is like I said this just the continuation of the of the plan and like you said uh all shout outs to to Kirk Cousins and I want to thank him personally for the in and out the the double double I got last when we got back from New York and he took whoever wanted to go to get a burger to celebrate the win. So, again, just a class act, a guy that really helped change that culture in that locker room. And those dividends should pay forward and then we'll see exactly what those lessons learned and how they were taken by Fernando. >> You know, everybody ties him along to Fernando Mendoza, but Tyler Lindbom, Colt Miller, Brock Bowers, Michael Mayer, Trent Tucker, all the players that had a chance to work with Kirk Cousins are going to be better off in years to come. But this is now Fernando Mendoza's team. We knew this would happen eventually and you and I debated on the radio and we've talked about it. Was it going to be the bye week? Was it going to be earlier? I've always said Kirk's going to play as long as he's playing well or there's an opportunity for the Raiders to make a decision at the trade deadline. They were able to do that. So, I think John Spytek, and he talked about it at the press conference, very tough decision. He wasn't planning on moving him until those phones started ringing and the team that wanted him the most was Minnesota. >> Yeah, it's a good problem to have because coming into the season when we saw the schedule release, that was literally the first thing we looked at, right? Well, when's the bye? Because that's the easy on-ramp for Fernando to come in and take over. Well, the fact that it's not until December, there is no easy on-ramp. And then you see the gauntlet, the schedule that they were on. Okay, well, do you really want to throw him in at that point if you're not making him the guy at the start? So, tough decision, but the best decision for the franchise moving forward is the is the way that John Spytek put it. And I can't disagree with him. Again, you cannot say enough about what Kirk Cousins did for this organization in these nine games. And really just a positive positive influence. And And he did They They've won more games already this year than they did all of last. So, I don't know what else you really could have asked for at this point from him. >> It takes two groups, two parties to make a deal and this deal doesn't happen if Carson Wentz doesn't play terribly on Monday Night Football and if Kyler Murray is healthy and he plays well. Kyler Murray is a two-time Pro Bowler, much younger than Kirk Cousins. He was supposed to be that franchise quarterback. I didn't think Minnesota panicked, but when they lost Monday Night Football and Justin Jefferson couldn't get his hands on the football. You could tell they were up all night in Minneapolis saying we got to make a deal and I think it's going to give them an opportunity in a very tough NFC North. I mean that division is a gauntlet the rest of the way and unless Minnesota wins a lot of games with Kirk Cousins they won't even make the playoffs. >> Well and that's the gamble that they're making there right is from the Vikings perspective they were willing to give up that third round draft pick because it's their own third round draft pick mind you. It's not the Eagles which which you think based on where the records are that would be the better draft pick. So you're looking at from the Raider perspective is essentially an early fourth rounder if the Vikings do what they hope to do and expect to do. But from their perspective he's a guy that that already knows the system. He knows that coach. He knows the market. He knows the team. He knows the city. So it was a no brainer for them so to speak. But again looking at it from the Raider perspective it was just simply time. >> I'm expecting a lot. I know Raider Nation is from Fernando Mendoza. He was the number one pick overall. He's the Heisman trophy winner. He brought his team Indiana to a national championship. That's not Notre Dame or Miami or a team that we used to see in that. He was born to be a leader. He's a leader within his family within this organization. Everyone speaks very highly of him and now he's going to come in and I think he's ready to play. You know Paul you and I have been covering football for a long time. There's a lot of first round picks that are thrown to the wolves but there's also a lot of hall of fame quarterbacks who struggled in their first year. Troy Aikman, Peyton Manning, John Elway. He gets an opportunity now to have at least a cushion of being behind Kirk Cousins and having Clint Kubiak to break him in. I'm expecting a high ceiling for him right out of the gate. >> Oh it should be. That That was the point of having him sit and learn at at the knee of Kirk Cousins and and really I I'm old enough You mentioned all those names. I'm old enough to remember those guys but I'm also young enough still to remember Carson Palmer when he sat out his entire rookie season. So for him to get a little bit of run, a little bit of burn at New England that that was some good things there that that he was able to get out there and and see how fast the NFL game is in a regular season situation. Now you're coming up against the the Super Bowl champions in the Seahawks. Doesn't get any tougher than that, but at least it's a home game. Uh the fans get the all week long to get ready for him and and again, it's just one of those situations where hurry up and wait. Okay, well now it's time. >> Yeah, you look at all those players who have been there in the past and who have had the opportunity to play. I'm fine. I am fine with Mendoza at week 10. We're good to go here. I think what the big question is what does this do for the Raiders offense as they move forward and they're going up against the world champs, the Seattle Seahawks. I think this opens up the deeper passing games where maybe Kirk couldn't make the longest throw possible. Fernando can make that pass much easily. I think the ball is going to zip in to Brock Bowers. Bowers should get the heavy targets. What is it going to mean to Ashton Denty with the wheel route in the passing game? And I wonder with him being under center or in the shotgun, what can this do to the running game? The running game hasn't done anything this year. With Fernando out there, will defensive coordinators now if he wants to spread it out say, oh my god, he's going to be trying to pick us apart. Let's get the running game going for the Raiders. >> Well, not only that, but he gives you that added added dimension of he can extend a play. He can take off and run for a 15 yd gain where where Kirk was not going to be able to do that. Plus the big arm. And And does that unlock somebody like a Trey Tucker? Does that unlock somebody like a Jaylen Nailor where again, no disrespect to Kirk, but but there were limitations to his game. What he was limited in physically, he more than made up for mentally, right? So now you're flipping that upside down and you're looking at it like this. It's like, okay, well what Fernando is going to be missing mentally, he's going to make up for physically. So you have to as a coach put him in those proper situations to to excel. Put him in a situation where he can succeed. And if he succeeds, then everyone else is going to be there. It's going to be real interesting to me to see who he potentially unlocks when it comes to the other guys on the roster. >> an outstanding point because he could make every throw. We knew that already at Indiana in the National Championship. We know he could make every throw in the NFL. I'm interested to see how big the playbook looks right out of the gate for him against a very good Seattle team and what they'll be able to do with him outside the pocket, inside the pocket. Remember where you were, Raider Nation, for this trade, because it could unleash a new look Raiders led by Fernando Mendoza. A lot more to come as we preview the Seattle Seahawks and the beginning of the Mendoza era on Raiders Weekly. Raiders Weekly is presented by Coors Light, mountain cold for Raider Nation. Celebrate responsibly, 2026 Coors Brewing [music] Company, Golden, Colorado. And by Spectrum, proud partner of the Las Vegas Raiders. Welcome back everyone to Raiders Weekly. Our Hall of Fame corner, Eric Allen joins us. And Eric, a lot of news with Fernando Mendoza now the starter. Kirk Cousins traded to Minnesota for a third round pick. When you heard the news, what did you think first about Kirk Cousins who brought a lot to the Raiders this year? >> Without a doubt guys, I I watched that Monday Night Game last night and and I'm pretty sure this is going to happen. Someone's going to be calling, particularly the Vikings for Kirk. And it's a great situation for everyone involved. I think the the management, the ownership, the player personnel people knocked it out the park as far as bringing Kirk Cousins in. I think it was an amazing opportunity for Fernando to be able to learn from a veteran and how to get it done on winning days and how to come back after difficult losses. I I think they did a great job. And then Kirk, I mean, had at one point this season leading the league in in touchdowns, was a great leader in the building early, out late. There's all the things that a veteran need to do, but at this point it's perfect for Fernando also to playing some meaningful football games as we approach week 10. >> Hey EA, from a player perspective, one of first questions that comes to mind and family members were asking me, what is this tell the rest of the locker room where you're four and five, you're right there around 500. He's having a great season. He's second in the in the league in touchdown passes, top five in passing yards. He's the face of the franchise, so to speak, at least offensively. What does that tell the locker room when you go ahead and move on from the quarterback at the middle of a season like this? >> Well, that's a great one, Paul. I think from outside, I think we have a lot of questions or the people from outside have a lot of questions about is he ready, you know, and what lessons does he learn and things like that. I think most of us on the inside have an understanding that he was ready, you know, and I mean, you're talking about a student of the game, does everything the right way, how he prepares, even, you know, sometimes you catch him on the sideline going through the play call because he had his helmet on listening to every detail that was going on. So I think he soaked up enough of the experience from outside the football field that he could do and at this point, there's nothing else he can learn not being on the football field. So I think it was a point that he was ready. Obviously, we know his physical capabilities. It was just the speed of the game, you know, that changes and I think he's going to be ready for that. >> You know, EA, it's really interesting that Clint Kubiak is so prepared. I don't know if he thought this was coming or not. This was a pretty quick trade, but he'll have him ready to go. So what do you think the Raiders want to see out of Fernando Mendoza in the first game considering he's going up against the world champions, a defense that is number one when it comes to limiting passing yards? They're just strong. They're stout from the defensive line to the back end at safety. This is going to be a big test for Fernando in his first game as a starter. >> Yeah, it sure will. And there's no doubt about that. They do a great job providing pressures at every level. They bring their safeties at time, their linebackers, their their defensive line is strong. They can two gap. They can kind of do everything that a coordinator would want to do to be successful that's really giving the quarterback difficult times. For our part, for the Raiders, though, we have a quarterback who gives the defense just a little bit of hesitation because he can extend plays outside the pocket. So if the edge is there and he's able to attack the edge and be able to get 10 yd, 15 yd on a running play to continue to sustain drives, I think that's going to be the one key that if I was the defensive coordinator facing this team without Fernando Mendoza, I could say I can pressure the Raiders from any point. I just want to get my hands up, force Kirk Kirk Cousins to be able to have to evade the pocket. Now I have to go back and kind of reorganize how I pressure this young quarterback because he's able to extend plays. And I just love the layered throws that we're going to see. And I understand Kirk was one of the best at those skinny posts, those slants early in the game. I mean, it was amazing how he was sticking those balls in there. But I think now that 20 to 25 yd area of the football field is going to be open for us. So again, you can have uh one of the tight ends drag across the middle and then have our uh slot receiver now be at about the 20 to 25 yd running some kind of dig or in cut, and that ball can get there on the money. And I don't think that's going to be that's not going to be an issue, and that's going to give Clint just another opportunity to really press the middle of the football field, which has been so successful for our Raiders so far. >> Yeah, I I know I think I know what the answer is going to be to this, but I'll I'll serve it up anyway. What do the Raiders need to do to keep the rookie quarterback out of those obvious passing situations where that defense, which is fearsome enough as it is, can't just sit back, pin its ears back and go after him? >> Yeah, I I think it's going to be really important to have those what we call extended run plays from the tosses to the running backs. And again, I go back to we were getting a little bit predictable the last week with Washington and on runs and Ashton in on passes. I think both of those guys would be able to hopefully be able to swing out of the backfield and have an extended run by just, you know, dumping it off early, kind of getting everyone kind of a feel for what we're trying to accomplish. So it's a safe throw. Now you have your running back on the edge able to maybe avoid one or two, get five or six yards. Now you're behind the chains, you're second and four, second and five. And then again, it's still all in the playbook. You can run it or throw it. So I think it's really important to utilize those running backs interchangeably. I don't want to see Ashton in on third down every time. I don't want to see Mike in on first down every time. You want to see them interchange and then utilize that young quarterback getting comfortable and getting a good feel by throwing those quick, easy kind of uh check downs to get him some completions early so he can then, you know, figure out a way to utilize that to be able to throw the ball down the field. >> You know, yeah, I think this first game jumps out at me because they got to get him going. Build some confidence with him. Typically with a first time starter, you get some screens going, you make some easy passes. The success when Cousins was here was the very fast quick passing game over the middle of the field. Stay with that. That's what Fernando saw on film when Cousins was completing those bullets over the middle to Brock. Now go back to Brock. You know Jackson Smith and Jaxon is going to get 12 to 15 targets. Have Brock have 12 to 15 targets. Make it easy on Fernando. Maybe sprint him outside, hit Brock as you talked about on a drag route. Let him get going with Brock Bowers, the best player on the Raiders to make it easy. And then I think Ashton Danty, who's getting hit a lot by the media for the running game, has been an outstanding catcher of the ball out of the backfield. Between Mayer, Brock, and Ashton, there should be a lot of easy throws even though it's a very good opponent. How do you see him making comfortable? Make him comfortable early in this game to get him in a rhythm. >> I I really do. I I think I'm all with that. The easy throws early, obviously you want to find a way to get Brock open early. Clint has done a masterful job of setting up uh plays where both tight ends, basically all three tight ends are a huge part of the football game. And if it's not Mike, of course it's big Brock. Ian also is in uh for some targets. Remember game two or three, he had a touchdown in the red zone, I believe. So the tight end room is really good and it gives you a great opportunity to get in a comfort ability situation with your quarterback, a young quarterback and your best tight end in the National Football League along with those backs. So if you continue to kind of feed him those easy targets early on, it builds confidence for him and then you're playing within the system. And I think that's the one thing that Clint has done and the last, you know, four or five weeks we really haven't paid a lot of attention to it, but if we go back to last week, I mean he chewed up the middle of the football field with Big Mike, with Brock. Just unfortunately we had some fumbles and things like that, but those routes have been open all year because of the design of the offense. And I really believe that uh Fernando is going to be able to step right in and still continue that rhythm that Clint has really produced for this offense. The one thing that was separating, I think uh keeping that young quarterback off the football field was the command that Kurt had in those short intermediate routes when guys were covered, putting it in a spot where only our receiver can get it. And then his decision making was really great. Unfortunately last week uh some of the decisions he made were not great, right? You when you fumble the ball you just want to toss that ball out of the end zone. You don't want to try a 50/50 ball with Trey Tucker. He's just not that kind of receiver. So again, when you're talking to talk about keeping a young player who has all that athleticism on the football field, I think this was the perfect opportunity for us to be able to include Fernando in this game. And I believe, guys, that that 25 to 30 yard space in the football field is going to open up a little bit more for us because of Fernando's arm strength and the ability of, you know, the inside receivers other than the tight ends to be able to get to those spots. >> Eric, last I just wanted to ask you about this too, going back from the player perspective. In many conversations I had with Jim Plunkett back in the day, he said that Al Davis used to always tell him, look, it doesn't matter how you play or how it looks, it only matters if we win. From a player's perspective, what does a successful Fernando Mendoza start look like on Sunday night? >> Well, I I think because you're going against the Seattle Seahawks and one thing that maybe we're all missing, I think it's really a great situation to match him up against a quarterback who also on the opposing team is Drew Lock, is not the Super Bowl champion or he's not an all pro guy. So we can now kind of compare quarterbacks, right? And see if he can outplay that quarterback. But I think being able to have control of the offense, the situations that present itself, just understand it and know what it's about and not, you know, I kind of look to the sideline that many times, those are the things that we're going to look for because your team feels that when you're on the football field. If you're feeling like you are controlling the situation, many situations are going to come up. Of course, he's going to get pressured from the edge and not know it. Is he going to recognize those things and evade it, extend the play, get out, make a big play on the edge of the football field? All those things are going to be judged. But when it comes down to it, Al Davis is right like he always is. It's all about winning. [laughter] It's all about getting the W at the end of the game. >> Well, we're going to have a great time at the Torch all of us because this is what Raider fans are waiting for, a historic moment. The Fernando Mendoza era begins and we do thank Kirk Cousins for a wonderful experience here, the way he treated us at training camp, the way we got to know him. We wish him well. EA, we'll see you Sunday. Uh thanks for joining us as always. >> All right, take care guys. >> There he is, the Hall of >> Famer, Eric Allen. He will be excited. I'm sure Fernando will be a part of his E's Keys at the Torch on Sunday. When we come back, Paul and I will wrap it up, give you our opinions on what needs to happen with a great opponent coming into Allegiant Stadium and the Raiders to have an opportunity to get back to 500 again. You're watching Raiders Weekly. >> Raider Nation, it's week 10 and the silver and black [music] are back at home at Allegiant to host the Seattle Seahawks. Here are three stats you need to know before kickoff. Number one, the number is seven. Brock Bowers has gone over 70 receiving yards in seven straight games to start his season. No tight end in NFL history has ever started like that. The only other tight end ever with a seven game streak of 70 plus yards at any point in the season is Rob Gronkowski back in 2014. Last week in San Francisco, Bowers caught seven of eight for 111 [music] yards and a touchdown. His 46 yards after the catch were the most on the team. Number two, well the number is [music] three. Max Crosby's sack of Brock Purdy came against Trent Williams, who had allowed just two sacks all season before that sack. Crosby forces quarterbacks to get the ball out fast. That sets up the [music] next number. The number is 2.41. That is Drew Lock's average time to throw in Seattle's win over Arizona, the quickest of his career. [music] He went 13 of 18 on quick passes and his best work came targeting tight ends and running backs. Arizona showed a blueprint [music] to hold Jackson Smith and Jaxon to a season low 51 yards, snapping his 13 game streak of 70 plus yards. Take away quick throws underneath and to the [music] back and the Raiders can make this a long day for Seattle's offense. Raider Nation, what are you tracking and what do you predict happens Sunday? >> [music] >> Raiders Weekly has been presented by Coors Light, mountain cold for Raider Nation. Celebrate responsibly 2026 Coors Brewing Company, Golden, Colorado. Welcome back to Raiders Weekly. JT, Paul Gutierrez from Raiders.com. You know, sometimes in sports everyone gets it wrong. So we spent a lot of time in July and August and all the talking heads at ESPN and Fox. When's Fernando going to play? It was either he's not going to play year one. He's going to play after the bye week. He's going to play when someone gets hurt. No one had the trade deadline with him going back to Minnesota where he's world famous over there. John Spytek pulled the trigger on the steal for a third round pick. And Paul, I really believe that this has got to be a defining moment. This has got to energize this entire locker room fan base, organization. Everyone in the building is excited for Fernando. >> Yes. >> waiting for and talking about. So the fact that he is now the guy, it's official. General Manager John Spytek and Coach Clint Kubiak both announced it. So there's no surprises here going forward, JT. He is the guy. The era begins and there's there's a certain symmetry that comes here. I know I mentioned earlier to EA about Jim Plunkett, but again, a Heisman Trophy winner, a guy that won in the Rose Bowl. I know that wasn't the title game back then, but and and was the number one overall pick. And oh yeah, there's the Latino factor there as well that I'm always going to pump up a little bit for for the guys too, but there's something special about Fernando Mendoza and the energy, the infectious energy that he brings to that locker room. And it's going to be a continuation of what Mr. Chains did, Kirgo Chains too. >> I also think our dear friend and legend Tom Flores is happy. And he's smiling for this one too because of the connection with Fernando. Now we see Seattle a very good team, world champs. They don't have Sam Darnold coming in and playing here, but they have Jackson Smith and Jigba. They have very good players and their defense is physical. The Raiders were on the field for 38 minutes defensively against the 49ers. They can't do that again. Someone's got to make a play. There are really good when I talked to Clint Kubiak and those great players on this team, Jacoby Dean, Kwai Walker, Max Crosby, A.J. Cole, you know, all the players that could come in like Brock Bowers, they're going to have to have a day. You cannot beat Seattle unless the stars align for the Raiders at Allegiant Stadium. >> And that's what was unfortunate about what happened in Santa Clara was when your steady Eddies are the ones that are having kind of the bad days, that that kind of derails what you want to do. So you need more than one of those stars to stand up and and take over the game so to speak. Be a game changer, be a game wrecker so that not every pressure is on Fernando Mendoza in his first ever start. And yet that 's where the storylines are going to be, right? Because that's the way the NFL is. The quarterback takes too much of the blame when things go wrong, too much of the credit when things go right. It's it's the nature of the beast. So I'm really excited to see exactly how the steadiest of the Eddies, Fernando Mendoza, handles all of this. >> Yeah, it's a great exciting time. You know, we look for excitement. This whole building's about history, Super Bowl trophies, the greatest players playing in the biggest games, and an opportunity to make history for Fernando. Um, but again, we're going to we're going to put a game plan together and we expect him to be able to play. What did you get out of it?
