So when the when the when it does come down to the a ball bouncing a certain way, we've maximized the chances to to for it to go our way, if that makes sense. And uh that's where I want our focus to be. >> On the radio is Demarcus Lawrence's best game maybe this year. What were you seeing out of him that really jumped out? >> Yeah, Daw, he's a um he played he played a great game. He really did. He I thought he um dominated his one-on- ons, played with incredible energy, running out of the stack, winning pass rushes, being dominant in the run game. Uh he's uh he's pretty he's pretty remarkable. >> Is he the type of, you know, Leo out and chatting out where he kind of takes that upon himself if he he needs to step it up? >> Probably a question for him, but I mean I I would have a hard time saying no to that, but uh yeah, your mind goes to okay, hey, guys are down. Who's t who's filling in the roles for them? Sometimes you overlook that it's more ops for the guys that have been playing. So, uh, but he he had a he had a really impressive performance. >> How how did you feel like Drew played given kind of the injuries he's going through and the constraints he had during? >> Yeah, Drew played really well. Drew played really well. I know like we didn't throw for a million yards, but thought he was efficient. He came up with some big time plays on third down um when we needed him and uh managed the game well with some of the stuff we were asking the quarterback to do. So, uh, having done that through all the other stuff I thought was, uh, was pretty awesome. >> What did lead to that efficiency we saw in the early downs from the offense? >> Well, if I said we were efficient, I'd pro I probably want to take that back. I mean, there's probably too many times we're in second long. Uh, but we did a great we converted on third down to keep those drives going. And so, uh, he did a great, Drew did a great job of keeping drives alive, keeping the ball moving forward, uh, converting on third downs. I thought he managed the situations great, like at the end of the half and two-minute and then in the four-minute situation. So, um, did a lot of good stuff on that end, but if we can be more efficient on those first and second down plays, I think that'll really help our offense as a whole. when you guys decide how much to blitz in any game, um how much of that's about what you guys are doing well and how much of that's about like what you see as an opportunity against the team you're going against? >> Uh yeah, both. Um >> how's it going Brady? >> Hey, what's up? >> Hey, good to see you. >> Um yeah, it's it's both. It's it's just a I have a hard time giving you like a steadfast answer on that one. It's just uh there's a lot of variables at play. Uh we want to be aggressive. I think I think we are at our best when we do pressure and there's a balance. You know, we have we have a really good front that we feel like can can play ball and we can play coverage behind it. But I'll also, you know, if you just sit in fourman fronts all day, that lets offensive lines tee off on those guys at a certain amount of time. So, you do need to be able to move uh you need to be able to change counts, things like that. you know, speed the quarterback up sometimes in some of the passing situations. So, uh, we have our philosophy. I think like the numbers kind of back that up, but I think I think it's fair to say that we're willing to fluctuate within a certain amount um, you know, from game to game or even within a game, you know, speed it up or slow it down. >> The running backs and the way they were used yesterday, is that kind of how you would see foresee it going forward now that both those guys are kind of healthy? >> Uh, saw it for how we wanted to use it yesterday. >> Yeah. Well, I mean, I guess that's kind of who I mean, Zach kind of started and then work to Darian and then in a little bit. >> Yeah. I mean, I think, you know, Zach's getting up to being about, >> you know, his play count keeps going up and up. So, um, I think I think it's fair to leave some flexibility based on game plan and how we feel each guy's playing, that sort of thing. So, and you know, with the other backs that are up, I mean, you know, they're ready to go as well. We've seen them play good football for us as well. But um I was happy with how our tail or our halfbacks played yesterday that I thought they um thought they did a nice job and I thought we felt some growth from from a week ago which was uh which is important. >> This managing of the practice reps for the quarterback, Mike, do you do does he do everything but throw? Is he in the huddle? Is he paniming behind the play? What does he not do or do? >> Well, he's he's not taking all the reps and he's not taking all the throws. uh how we manage it is kind of a day-to-day thing based off of how he's feeling and like maybe like the aggregate that we're going to shoot for for a whole week. But um there's some there's some such situations where we want him to be in there and not throwing. There's some situations where you know Jaylen's in there doing everything as well. So it's just kind of it's kind of a a mixture from day to day. >> Did you feel as a staff almost blind how this might work out yesterday and now going forward this week you know how he handled it and how it came out in the game. much more. >> Well, we felt like it we we were optimistic that it wasn't going to be a we knew he was going to be sore coming after the game, but we didn't we also felt like we were optimistic that uh it wasn't going to be a long-term thing. It was really like a week- toeek thing. Hey, let's let's let's do our best to get him ready for this game, go play the game, and then we'll kind of re-evaluate as we go into this week. So, we'll definitely take how we handled it last week into consideration on how we translate that into this week. Um, >> yeah. >> How much flexibility do you build in a game plan when you're trying to figure out what he may or may not be able to do on Sunday, whether it's getting the ball downfield or what feels comfortable to him? >> Yeah, those things are always taken into account. Uh we felt like um yeah, I mean it's just those are things you have to consider, right? It's just do we really want to explain what we feel like we didn't want to be able to do? Probably not. But uh but that's just that's part for the course, you know. So, I think our I think our staff did a great job both uh throughout the week having a plan for Drew and Jaylen and then also in game being able to make adjustments on what we felt like we could we could get to and uh it's also in response to how we feel like we're being played and what the guys are executing well as well. >> You said uh last week that analytics has made it really easy or easier for people to self scout and that tendencies are kind of going away to some extent. Do you do you feel that way? And has that affected the way you approach a game plan um in terms of of when you call certain plays? >> Uh yeah. Yeah. Um there like analytics is such a wide variety of like what that I mean it's anywhere from just like you're looking at run pass numbers and you're looking at like effectiveness numbers on one end of the spectrum. you know, you have all these advanced metrics nowadays and then you have you kind of bucket things in terms of operational things that you look at. So, uh, to me, you're always looking at it through like multiple lenses, what they've done, where you feel like they're going, and how we've been attacked, and how that applies to, uh, how we feel like the team's going to play us. and you kind of divvy up, you know, you attribute certain percentages kind of each bucket based off the situation. Is it an exact science? No. I think sometimes we're right and it's great and we're in a great defense or a great call and sometimes we're wrong and we got to make adjustments or we got to get through the down. So, um, maybe we need to do it better. I don't know. It doesn't sound like we're doing it very well. I know we asked you about Nick after the game, but looking at the tape and just kind of overall the job he did, particularly on McBride, just what did you think of his game? >> Yeah, we asked him to match up a few times and uh he did a great job. He did a great job. Um I think he had a great mentality throughout the week. He was on his details and I think you saw that kind of manifest itself in the game by him just letting it rip and and uh and playing a great game. I mean, we asked him to blitz, we asked him to cover. Uh, obviously the play in the red zone was was awesome and then uh we had a plan for him to rush as well. We just weren't able to get to some of those situations that we wanted to. >> What do you think of the offensive line play overall with Gray and Anthony going back into their old spots there? >> Yeah, I thought I thought our guys played hard. Um, like to see our run game be more effective on in some of these uh early down type of situations. I think that's going to I I would expect it to uh vastly improve after another week like full week of reps with those guys in those spots and understanding their role going into the game. So uh I appreciate the effort, the toughness, but uh I feel like I feel like there's room for improvement. >> You you've talked a lot about the depth having to play in that game and just all the different guys. Connor Aul didn't practice at all last week. It's pretty rare for a guy to not practice, especially a young guy, and then play. Like what do he show you just to make it to the game and be able to contribute? Yeah. I mean, let's just there's things that he had to be willing to to do to uh get himself ready and and he uh was a and he did those things, which is not an easy thing to do. So, uh tip of the cap to Connor. He's um tough guy, great teammate. um thought he went in and executed well really in in both phases and uh and he played hard, you know, so uh that's all you really can ask the guys and I think I think that shows through the rest of the the guys on the tape when they see what Connor does when he goes in there and just letting it rip. So, um yeah, hats off to him. >> And I know you addressed this on the radio, but do you have any clear idea of what happened on the play with when Sundell got the penalty and why they spotted the ball, how they did there? to my knowledge, the reason it went back is because of offsetting penalty and then the uh the personal foul play trumps the uh the 5- yard play, which I think that's like the is that like the second or third time it's happened to us. >> Yeah. I think we had a face mask maybe a year or two ago when they >> overcame another fiveer. So, um, yeah, that just was didn't go our way. you know, we had an opportunity to really go ahead in the game, but uh that was a bummer. >> Mike, you've talked about the importance several times of players getting ahead of the play. Can you expand a little bit of what that is and why it's important as a collective to be ahead of? >> Well, let us be connected. So, got one one guy's thinking, you know, that we're doing this and another guy's thinking we're doing that. Well, you're not together. So, that's that's in all phases. That's uh happens all the time on teams in terms of either how we're blocking something or how or how we're actually defending a certain type of return, how we're relating to people. It happens on offense and how we're protecting and routes we're running and how we're targeting in the run game. And on defensively, you know, the way that we operate. Um it's very important that we get our cleats in the ground and we're all looking at the right stuff so when the ball snap, we can go play. um we've done a great job of that in all three phases and but I think uh when you look at yesterday and some of the success that um the other team had that uh we felt like we could have been in better positions to uh make it more difficult for them. >> Mike, with the injuries to to Sam and Drew, this is the closest you've been to needing to go to Jaylen for any for any stretch of play. How have you kind of feel like he's progressed getting the the run of practice reps last week and kind of where his whole game is at at this point as you >> Yeah, Jen was ready to go yesterday. Um, I'd say the probably the biggest difference that I've seen was him having an opportunity to take, you know, reps with the ones throughout the week with the starters and uh you just you felt the poise, you felt a a uh a confidence in how he was operating, a decisiveness on him delivering the football and then um a lot of good stuff honestly during practice. So, obviously we were rolling with Drew. Um Drew's earned that opportunity. and he's played great football for us when he's been out there, but if he wasn't able to go, we're we're confident in Jaylen. >> How did you arrive at your philosophy about how to balance, you know, confusion that maybe uh coverage disguise causes the offense versus potentially having guys that need to get to a position that's a little harder at postnap rotation? >> Well, uh not every situation is the same. Um, we've we've we've messed around with like a bunch of pre- snap rotations on early downs and it uh it's hard to like manage all that stuff, you know, like you're going to call it and this call we want to be like this and it's gets wordy and gets gets unwieldy. So, you know, we we've evolved to a a too high defense with with change ups and and then uh by situation. We have ways that we want to be able to show certain presentations, but um I think that falls in like the hey, we want to live we want to live in our our wheelhouse of what we feel like our core competencies are and what our guys are used to executing and we can do it at a high level. However, we feel like as coaches, you know, the best we can tailor that to attack the way we want to attack certain off, you know, how offenses operate and certain people, then uh that'll help our players as well. So, it's like you can do things full speed that are also hopefully, you know, schematically advantageous for your guys so they they feel like they have the upper hand. So, that's the lens that we look at it through. >> Uh Drew got the ball out really quickly yesterday, didn't get sacked, only took a couple hits, but you also didn't have many explosive passing plays. Were you willing to sort of trade make that trade-off or is there a way to have both? >> I think there's a way to have both. Yeah. >> How do Anthony Bradford played this return? >> I think just like I said with the rest of the line, I think he played hard. Um had some had some really good physical plays that uh that really only a guy like AB can do that he brings that what he's unique to what he brings to the table. And there's also uh plays where we need to be more connected on the offensive line and making sure that um we got the right people accounted for so we can go run off the ball and and play the way that I know our our guys know how to play. So um this week will be really helpful knowing that he's got all the reps and he's starting and we know who's going to be where and I expect I expect everyone to take another step. >> And is Nelson's surgery imminent or do you know what's >> I believe it was today actually. >> He had it. >> Yep. Does that is he on sort of the Sam Darno we hope to return after the buy type of deal or is that a longer term? >> Uh well it's not we're not put on IR yet. So I think that gives you the timetable of what we expect. Consider it week to week I guess best way to put it. >> Anything else? Thank you. >> All right. Thank you. >> Thank you. Thank you.

Uh always room for improvement, but with with the movement that we've had across our line in the last two weeks to kind of come together and especially finish the game the way they did was um really cool. >> You said your defense as a whole had the long [clears throat] drive to start the game and then score again after that. >> Yeah, uh we're just talking to less about it. It's just like the composure of our team, like the togetherness. There's a lot of there's several things that didn't go our way today and I felt like we got the ball out several times. Um there are some penalties that that were against us to kind of put us in some not some not great situations, but just no flinch from the fellas. Sometimes he's kind of uh at the end of the progression and when the ball finds him, you know, if you can make a guy miss, you know, it's it's like a great example. I think he's just going to continue to get better um now that he's kind of stacking weeks and he's and he's getting healthier uh that'll help us. >> And you talked about trying to play Seahawks football and uh outside of the penalties maybe um how did this game grade for you in that regard? >> Yeah, I thought I thought we took a step today. title: Drew Lock: "This Building Is So Special" | Seattle Seahawks
text: Here we are. Let's do it. >> But Jalen, how are you feeling? I was told that you suffered an oblique injury as well during the game. >> Yeah. Um, I don't know, we'll get it looked at tonight. Um, I was able to finish with it, but you know, we'll get it looked at and um, go from there, but not too bad. >> Was it on that in-completion to Jameson Williams? >> Yeah. Yeah, it was a scramble. Or not a scramble, it was a movement, it was a keeper. Um, I think it was third-ish quarter, maybe. >> How did it affect you? >> Uh, I wouldn't say it did. Um, went into the tent, had it looked at, came back out, just let me see how it feels throwing the ball. I was like, "Wait, I've already I've already thrown the ball." He was like, "All right." Went through it. I mean, you feel it, but it's nothing that you know, is going to keep me on the sideline. >> What about the elbow injury? How was it playing through that? >> Uh, good. Um, you know, I I I mentioned it um, out on the field, I believe, but the staff here, the training staff, the strength staff, Coach Mike, like everybody handled it so great today this week. Jalen Milroe, um, it was I think it was really well done. Um, just just hats off to to this building, to this team, um, for being able to you know, stick with me throughout this week and get us here to Sunday as as healthy and as ready as we could we could be. >> You kind of you kind of downplayed the amount of limited you were when we talked to you on Thursday, but your teammates have said you know, you only had so many throws and all that. Just how hard was getting ready or what was kind of the key to being prepared for this game when you weren't able to get full reps? >> Yeah. Um, >> [clears throat] >> you know, I would say the walk-throughs are obviously huge. you know, everybody understanding that I I wasn't going to throw during those. with us playing on a Monday night, being able to do a walk-through practice Wednesday, you know, not throw there. Um I think it all, like I said, the building, coaching staff, strength staff, training staff, all you know, having a piece in on this, um was fantastic. It It really It really worked well. And to go back to probably something I've said before, but I feel like I've found my way as a guy that doesn't get reps as a backup to be ready for a game and um so when we got to this week, it was you know, it's not something that I wasn't used to, to say the least. Um just mentally being as prepared as I can with tape, walk-through reps, rewatching practices, and and being ready to come out here and spin it around. >> So, is the takeaway that practice is over with? >> No, but you can kind of click into the well, we don't ever really fully practice on Thursday nights, so we go out and play on Thursday night games and kind of talk to yourself that way, so. >> How much did you throw this week compared to what you would in a normal week when you would be starting? >> Yeah. Um now the the the only balls I threw were on Thursday. Um and I we did a little bit of a split there, but say I took majority of the reps Thursday and and that was it. >> It looked like you didn't throw much pregame. Like you kind of just came out >> Yeah, I know. They They had a again a great plan discussed basically all day Saturday on how we wanted to handle this. And uh yeah, that it was executed perfect. Hats off to everybody and um yeah, waited to throw until finally got the shoulder pads and helmets on. >> Was it kind of similar to what you saw Sam kind of deal with in in the playoffs last year? Like how the lead up and management kind of went with that? >> It's basically the same template. Um a a like a 3-minute tweak in the middle of it, but that was it. Yeah, they been through it before the previous and again, going back to your question, seeing Sam do it in the previous year and not practice, I was practicing for him, then him being able to come out on a Sunday and and play really, really good football out throughout the playoffs, was was uh something I I hang my hat on it I could, you know, model model myself this week on on what he did. >> Did you feel pretty dialed like right from the jump or did it take a little bit of time to kind of get up to speed with that? >> Um no, I'd say I'd say I felt pretty good going into it. Um you know, the arm felt fresh, it felt good, you know, to start the game and that's kind of all the confidence I needed to be able to go out and not think about it and just play football. >> This is only the second game this year that Zach and JD have been able to play together. Just between the physicality and then the you know, JD's ability to make guys miss. Just how much were you feeling both of them in this >> Yeah. Um you know, I'll I'll probably get in trouble for a couple reps, but handing it off, not doing a fantastic, you know, keeper out cuz I was looking back and watching Zach and JD run sometimes. They were fighting through contact. First guy wasn't tackling. The line was making great holes, tight ends. I mean, it was it was classic run game from Zach and and JD tonight. along with our offensive line just playing their butts off, man. It was so fun. >> Yeah, just your injury situation, obviously, you guys were missing a bunch of guys on both sides of the ball today. And to win the way that you did with the physicality and ball control and all that kind of stuff. Just how gratifying is it to see the way that you guys were able to control the game? you know, Mike preaches it. Uh the ready squad, you know, it's 70 guys ready to roll at at at any time. Um it's kind of just a mentality that this building has. Um so, we knew that whoever it was, stepping up, playing their first game, playing their 100th snap, whatever it was, guys were going to be ready, guys were going to be focused. Coaches have to do a great job of of putting together a plan on both sides of the ball for guys that haven't played maybe all year. Um it's is awesome. It I keep going back to it, but this building is so special. This coaching staff, going into games, you feel confident as you've ever been. And uh we can just keep doing that, keep progressing, and keep getting better. The sky's the limit. >> This the drive before that uh but look like you guys got really aggressive after maybe you got that first first down and started throwing it downfield. Was that Was that just kind of plan there, or did you see something there, or >> No, I think [sighs] it it's just flurry, feeling the game, feeling it out, and you know, like as it as it always is, my job to go out and execute, and operationally get us up to the ball, keep the false starts minimal, and when he calls it down field, I'm going to take it, and drop back, I'm going to take it, quick game, we'll we'll go from there, and I think it's just flurry feeling it. >> After the opening injury, were there any throws you really felt it, or that you felt like you couldn't make because of the injury? >> No, it's it's a crazy experience of you know, being out there, and just not feeling anything, adrenaline, how important it is, it just kind of goes away, you kind of don't think about it until you come sit down on the sideline, and go, "Yeah, that's that's still there." Um no, that I didn't feel like there was anything I couldn't couldn't do in as far as throwing goes, so I relayed that to the sideline, and we just kept moving forward. >> It's cliche around the league, but now that's three games you haven't turned the ball over. How much with this defense are you Is that really what it comes down to? If you take care of the ball, the defense is going to win the game. >> Um I I know that that's a big um a big thing for me going into every week, um knowing that we can control the game with the run, you know, operate on third downs well, keep the ball in our hands, allow our defense to have, you know, long fields to defend, not giving the team the ball on the 30, or the 20, or whatever, and maybe even at the 50. Um playing complimentary We have the best punter in the world, so getting to fourth down, it is what it is when you have, you know, Michael Dickson being able to punt, and pin guys deep, and allow our defense to have a a 90-yard, you know, cushion, so to say. >> Through that first touchdown drive, uh J'Tarrian and Zack combined for 53 of the 55 yards on the drive. Just to see a running back group that's kind of maybe struggled to find its full self this year as a collective, to kind of put together that kind of a a drive for you guys, and contribute that much. How how How big can that be to maybe springboard this that whole unit going forward? >> Yeah, those guys are they're the workhorses of this team. I think it says a lot about the running back room in general knowing that we didn't have Sharps early in the year. We lost JD to the IR. With E-man and and George and even Valas being able to step up, make plays when their number is called. To be able to then get Zach and JD back. Zach having a couple games under his belt now after a very serious injury obviously is you're just going to keep seeing him come come more and more to life. Hats off to that room. All of them have had their number called at some point and they have personally my opinion they've all been ready. yeah, they're just huge for us. >> You hit some tight passing windows over the middle of the field. What did those mental reps what role did they play in you being able to do that despite not having all the practice time off? I think it I think it I mean I'll actually I'll give you the real truth. That first drive uh similar route to Jacks kind of threw it in front of him a little too much. And we had a conversation on the sideline and I was like, "Look, dude, I was ready for you to kind of like rip through there and then run into that." And he's like talking to me about the safety and the backers and the holes and he's feeling like he's going to sit up a little bit. I was like, "All right." He did exactly what he told me he was going to do those next couple times we ended up running that route and I went up to him after that drive and I said, "Never ever let me tell you how to run a route again cuz you keep doing what you're doing, tell me where you're going to be and we'll make it work." >> So, are you pretty confident you'll be able to play next week if you >> Yeah. Yeah. >> Anything else? Thank you. >> Thanks.

title: Julian Love: "The Seahawks Style Was Definitely Present Today" | Seattle Seahawks
text: How we doing? >> Good. >> Mike said he felt like you guys maybe got some of your swagger back today or whatever. That felt like more of that kind of game. Did did it feel like that to you? >> For sure. I mean, it's hard not to look at like the result of it. Um but I think the feel during the game just it felt like us. Um offense was doing their thing. Drew Lock played a great game. Running backs ran their butt off. Um and uh yeah, the O-line played ball. And then on defense, we we run to the ball. We were I think pretty violent today, which was was fun to see. Um got to be cleaner, of course. We're always going to say that, but the the the swagger, the Seahawk style was definitely impressive today. >> Then 89 yd on that first drive and >> Yeah. >> like 100 some yards the rest of the way. So what changed, if anything, after that first drive to really settle in then? >> I feel like I I got to go back to that drive. Uh but I feel like it was just a lot of stuff on us. Just being clean. Uh first series kind of jitters maybe for some guys. Just being the right calls. Um right checks. Uh there's just a few just mishaps. Uh and so you go to sideline after that and I think the team that we are, the defense we are, it's like okay, we just gave them 80 89 yards. We gave them 89 yards. Um that's kind of the swagger and ego we kind of have. Um especially if it's true. Uh then you go out and yeah, we we shut them down the rest of the game. >> When you come into a game and you're missing the guys that you're missing and you're coming off a loss and you kind of have that thought of something to prove maybe. I mean, do you enjoy that? I mean, obviously you never you never want to have guys be down. >> Just with something to prove. Like does that add anything? >> Yeah, I mean, I think I'll give you the coach speak uh answer first. Um that was a full 70 game. I'm sure Mike came up here and said it took all 70. Uh you guys have seen that in Hard Knocks um about kind of how we operate. But then just like as a person who's been in some of those role been in that position to step in and like get your time, your opportunity, I think guys took it on themselves like, man, I'm not like filling in for somebody. I'm going to make my opportunity shown here um or known here. And yeah, I think guys on both sides of the ball did that. We had some a lot of young guys playing today and guys who are going to be household in a few years. And so it's cool to see them get their shine in a big game, division game, and really just own the moment. And so it's it's just really cool to see it. As me as a leader, just try to be just very stout and just be kind of that that pillar that people can lean on. But the guys, man, they were they were balling. It was pretty easy for them. >> What is it about even worry that you can just stick him on one of the best tight ends in the league on third and fourth down? >> He's he's special, man. He you can't pigeonhole him into anything. Whether he's hitting the quarterback, whether he's in coverage, he just he's such a problem. And it's a mixture of God gifted, just being so tall, arms long, so fast and strong. But then just his mental, man. It's it's not easy. I think it might get really overlooked how smart of a player he is because he's doing so much. Not everyone on our team can be doing that. And so yeah, can't speak highly enough. He should be talked about in a in a special sort of way. >> When you know the call is locking him up on McBride, you know [clears throat] do you feel like you don't even have to look there? Do you you got other >> Yeah, for sure. I think you know, obviously out there today, McBride's a good player. But in general, yeah, you you feel confident in your guys. He's he's matched up on people for a reason. And they had, you know, Wilson and McBride were two dynamic players. I thought we did a great job on them today. I give catch at the end. I'm bummed about but for the most part, we had a good game plan and we we applied it. >> I saw you high five Chardonnay after that 25 yard catch that got negated. But just the style that he is with, what does that do for you guys when you see just the violence that he kind of brings? >> Man, that was a play. That was I was I mean, that was like first half Beast Quick for for a hot second. That was impressive. And I don't know, that's just a swagger and energy. I'm you know, whether it's you know, him doing the play or our sidelines erupting, like that it all snowballs. I think just ball finds energy and yeah, that was a that was a fun play, man. It's it's really cool to see him work for so long, just not complain. He's such a good dude. Everyone loves him. And then just he he just falls right back in place and just being a dynamic running back for us. I thought played a great game as well. Um and so it's really cool to see the vibe and the the energy of that running back room right now. >> What what was it like seeing Drew kind of go through what he had to do to get ready ready this week or did he suffer another injury and kind of play through that? >> Yeah, that dude's a beast, man. He's so tough um and just so cool. Like he nothing phases him no matter what. He's just he's confident. He has swagger. He really he plays offense like a defensive player. I think that's why all of us really love him, especially on defense. Um and I don't know we just there's confidence there. Um I've said it for for years now. He's the best two in the game. Um uh we're we're really happy to have him on our team. >> 11 straight wins over the Cardinals. I mean that kind of success over one NFL team over another pretty unprecedented. I mean what is it about year in year out game year year to year that you just continue to have this kind of success for division rival? >> Yeah, it's crazy. That's a crazy number. Um I think it it's kind of the opposite what you would think. I feel like especially these past like you feel like a couple years they have dynamic players and they have momentum always coming into playing us. And so it's like they're never overlooked. Like we are as charged up and as on the details playing these guys as everybody else in the division. Like because they present some serious stuff and they have they have a lot of good players on their team. [clears throat] And so it's that mindset I think what makes it special. It's not like uh like you're you're looking down on any team. Um you we're very prepared uh for these guys. We know their style. We know they can make plays. Um we just we know it's going to be a battle. It was a battle for most of this game. Uh we were able to pull away. Um and so I think it's that mindset that makes this um that number kind of is crazy. >> Drew, I know there's a mindset obviously the in the red zone. How much of mindset was that try to say let's not get them in the red zone? You know what I mean? Go from there. >> I mean judging by my uh I play there in that that fourth quarter I wanted them to get in the red zone just so we can get our numbers right. No, I didn't. I'm kidding. Um I don't know. I mean teams are going to get in the red zone. Like yeah, we want to stop them. want to force outs. We want to get turnovers, all that stuff. But the make and the mark of a good defense is stopping them no matter what. You can pull up the ball You can put the ball down wherever and we're going to play until the last snap. Defend the blade of grass is kind of the the mindset. And so it's cool to to have two opportunities to show that. We've been putting a ton of work in our red zone defense. We needed to. We We're not We're We were not very good at it. Um and so we want to put on this play that we're turning this thing around. >> Commenting football, you do stop them in the red zone, then your offense takes the ball for the last four minutes and lights out. >> No, it's big time. That I mean the the Zach's runs uh drew that that QB sneak to get him out of the backed up. Um that's just I mean that's style right now. That If you want to get uh Mike McDonald smiling, just talk about that sequence of plays. Um fourth down stop in the red zone and offense just kind of imposing their will in the run game. Uh that's uh Yeah, that's the Seahawk way. >> Julian, you talked about imposing the will. There was a time in the third quarter when no one on the defense had more than three tackles. How does that speak to your game tackling? >> That's a That's kind of crazy. Um That's crazy. Uh I don't know. It's No one ever thinks that way. We kind of move as a wave. We're kind of a swarmy solid defense. I think that's what makes us fun. Um and I think that's what makes offenses really not like playing us because it's like, all right, we have some talented players, of course. Um but we're going to get to the ball. Uh we have each other's backs. People are going to miss sometimes, but you're going to have two, three more Seahawks you know have to the ball. And so kind of crazy and pretty cool. >> Anything else? >> Appreciate y'all. Thank you. >> Thank you.

title: REACTION: 49ers TRADE for Keenan Allen...
text: Happy trade deadline day. I know many of you were anxious. You wanted some sort of movement. Well, the 49ers have traded for six-time Pro Bowl wide receiver Keenan Allen. So they continue doing business with the Indianapolis Colts and not for a high price for a 34-year-old wide receiver who played his college ball here in the Bay Area for Cal in Berkeley. I say not a high price. This is the exact price for Keenan Allen, a sixth-round pick in the 2027 draft. 49ers have all but their fourth-round pick entering this trade because they sent that one to Indy for DeForest Buckner. Keenan Allen is going to cost the six. He had a $1.3 million veteran minimum base salary. So you prorate that. Nine games left for the 49ers, so just over half the season. That is about $688,000 in base salary and up to $270,000. That's $30,000 per game in per-game roster bonus money. So Keenan Allen is a 49er, the 34-year-old very accomplished wide receiver. And we could go ahead and put this right on the depth chart right now. I'll open it up here in just a second. Just want to talk a little bit about Keenan, who's been in the league for a long, long time. Started with the San Diego Chargers back in 2013. And as I said, six Pro Bowls. It's a tall receiver. We know that Brock Purdy is so accurate that the tall receivers I think it's like a force-multiplying thing when Brock Purdy's your quarterback because he's able to put the ball where only the guys who are 6'2 and above can get it. And Keenan Allen is 6'2. He's obviously played the X over the course of his career. You look at Mike Evans. You need Mike Evans. Mike Evans is still at the top of the game despite the age, but you're also managing Mike And this is buys you more time to allow you to manage Mike Evans. So, Keenan Allen is I think the the bridge for the 49ers to ensure that Mike Evans does have enough time to get this Achilles settled down and then you use Mike for the biggest games this season, almost an NBA load management situation. Allen was with the Chargers from age 21 until 31, a full decade with the Chargers, moving from San Diego to LA. He was Joey Bosa's teammate. Maybe Joey Bosa will join him on the 49ers later this year if Joey's been working out. We can talk about that later though. Went to the Bears in 2024, back to the Chargers in 25 with the Colts this year. He can play the big slot. And I think especially at this age, Keenan Allen at age 34, I think that you might see him inside more often than outside. That you know, outside you talk about speed needing the win or size. And I know Mike Evans he's he's a wizard. He's a separator. He can win anywhere. The 49ers have been using Evans a lot inside in the slot this year. And this offense is going to be you know, I call it ambidextrous, I call it versatile, I call it adaptable. Every receiver has to be able to play every single spot. If you are going to bring somebody in, and the 49ers obviously are bringing Keenan Allen in, that receiver needs to be able to pick the playbook up quickly. And you know, I I think you rule out a lot of possibilities who you know, kind of fringe guys on the on the trade market just by virtue of that fact, right? Because it takes a while to pick up this playbook. It takes a while to earn chemistry with Brock Purdy. Look how quickly the vets, like the guys that played a lot of football like a Mike Evans have been able to find rhythm with Purdy. And you know, I also talked earlier today if the 49ers weren't able to find value at wide receiver, I earlier today I said maybe Dallas Goedert from Philadelphia, pass catching tight end because you lost Jake Tonjus in week one of this season would help the passing offense. Just a bigger body who can catch the football, may not be a top speed anymore. Keenan Allen I think fits that role. I mean so much of this is amorphous, right? The wide receivers play tight end, the tight ends play wide receivers. You need your receivers to block. You see Keenan Allen there, big body. It's funny that Jordan Schultz used the 13 jersey. Obviously Keenan Allen is not going to be wearing number 13 with the 49ers. Neither did Mike Evans. Mike Evans of course changed to the number five. So we'll see what Keenan Allen wears for San Francisco, but he's got 40 catches this year. And he's been fairly available player over the past few seasons with the last season that that he went under 11 games of availability was in 2022. Played 13 games in 23, 15 games in 2024, 17 games in 2025. Played a full season in 2025 with 81 catches and 777 yards. And this year through eight games for the Colts, not a great situation over there in Indianapolis, 40 catches, 351 yards for Keenan Allen with a touchdown on the season. So I mean he still can produce and he's not going to be asked to carry a massive load with the 49ers. Again, layering depth at wide receiver is what has been very important. And yes, this now officially, if it wasn't already, probably is the oldest offense of all time. But remember what Mike Evans told me before we took off to Australia to cover the 49ers. I was in the locker room. I was talking to Mike and I mean this was casual, no cameras out there or anything. Uh we were just talking about the age and and experience and how, you know, on offense experience, I think especially in this case with the 49ers, trumps the the age concerns. And Mike just kind of smiled at me, and he said, yeah, we're old, but we can ball. Keenan Allen, 34, like Evans, old, but he can ball. And I'm not saying that Mike Evans is 34, but I'm saying that these are older players. Mike Evans, self-admittedly, is an older player. George Kittle on the other side of 30. Christian McCaffrey turned 30 this off season. You could go up and down. Deebo Robinson go up and down this 49ers receiving room. They are the number two offense in football with a chance to be the number one offense in football before all is said and done, despite the fact that they're dealing with this age. And I think that the precision that comes from the experience and the the know-how of how to pick up the playbook and experience having seen different systems, I think has worked very very well for the 49ers this season. While they're the oldest offense in the NFL, they're one of the younger defenses in the league, and it's obvious how they're building the team and how they're pushing the chips into the middle of the table this year. They they have the the MVP. Brock Purdy's been the best quarterback in the league. You give him what he needs to succeed. You layer the depth at the receiving position, and we can now officially add Keenan Allen to the 49ers depth chart. So how does this work? Because right now, obviously, there are 53 on here. Somebody's going to have to be removed. We'll see if there was an injury. We'll see if they'll cut somebody. Many questions are going to be answered. Brandon Aiyuk is technically on the team right now, but the 49ers have a two-week roster exemption for Brandon Aiyuk. By the way, I'm going to share an update on that Brandon Aiyuk situation in just a second. But I you know, this really really helps move Deebo Samuel into the Joker gadget role permanently. And it had always been a worry that if you had too many receivers hurt that Deebo Samuel would have to play the Z, or Deebo Samuel would have to play a set F position. And then Deebo Samuel is asked to separate a little bit too much. And then I think that if Deebo Samuel's a standard wide receiver, I think you're defeating the point, defeating the purpose of Deebo Samuel. I think that you want him to be that joker. You want him to be that guy that is roving around the formation, that is finding mismatches, that can be the gadget weapon, a glorified gadget weapon. And therefore, Keenan Allen will slot into the starting F position, the big slot position for the 49ers. You're going to be able to block really well with him, and you're already the number one rushing offense in the league in terms of success rate. And he also gets the teal highlight right there as a trade or a free agent acquisition. So the fit is very, very natural for the 49ers. The price is low for San Francisco. Again, a sixth round pick, $688,000 in base salary and up to $270,000 in per game roster bonus money for Keenan Allen. 49ers right now have the oldest wide receiver to catch a pass this season, and they have three of the four oldest wide receivers to catch a pass this season. Mike points out that Keenan Allen has yet to be suspended for his DUI arrest on August 30th. So at some point, there's going to be a mandated three-game suspension by the NFL's collective bargaining agreement. And this is going to be a good I I had figured that that suspension had already been served, but this is a good point. He was arrested on August 30th, .224 blood alcohol reading. And the NFL could also suspend him for longer than three games. I would be very surprised if the 49ers didn't have some sort of idea as to when discipline might come down before making this trade, but that's obviously going to be a question for John Lynch and Kyle Shanahan once this is officially ratified. As of right now, I don't have any more information on that front. But three of the four oldest receivers to catch a pass this season are with the 49ers and all four are in the NFC West. Keenan Allen, the oldest, now with the 49ers. Davante Adams with the Rams, but hurt right now. Mike Evans with the 49ers and Brandon Cooks with the 49ers. And yes, Keenan Allen did go to school at Cal. He is a former Cal Golden Bear. That was a long time ago. I covered him back in college. He was in the Pac-12 before Christian or the I mean yeah, it was the Pac-12 already. I think he transitioned from the Pac-10 to the Pac-12 during his time in college. But that was before Christian McCaffrey was even at Stanford. I mean that was the end of the Jeff Tedford era at Cal. I I'm trying to go back to his college career here from 2010 to 2012. Yeah, 46 catches as a freshman. We even have a picture here of Keenan Allen playing for the Cal Golden Bears. He was a monster in in college as you would expect from somebody who's been in the NFL for such a long time. He's made this a nice productive career. Again, six Pro Bowls. Uh that is no laughing matter. That is Keenan Allen playing a home game back at Memorial Stadium sometime between 2010 and 2012. Going through I'm going to go through some of his career numbers here. He's obviously delivered several 1,000-yard seasons. His rookie year with San Diego and I'm guessing Philip Rivers in 2013. 2017, 2018, 2019, 2020, 2021, I would consider that his prime. In 2020 he missed the 1,000-yard mark by eight yards. And uh the most recently hit 12:43, 1,243 yards in 2023 with the Chargers. Good route runner, savvy guy to be in the league for this long, 14 seasons in the NFL, 12,402 receiving yards in the regular season and made the playoffs four times. In the postseason, three touchdowns for Keenan Allen and a 1,000 yd pace by the way in the postseason. So he has produced in the postseason and the 49ers do plan to be there. But the the goal here is to build that bridge to Mike Evans to make sure that you've got a receiver with size and with presence to give Mike Evans as much time as possible to ramp up, to make sure you're not putting undue pressure on that Achilles. You give Brock Purdy another tall target and you know, let me just re-emphasize how good this 49ers offense has been this year. We can look at the team tier chart on Ben Baldwin's website. This is where the 49ers are as a team. The offense now has surpassed Buffalo's actually. I was saying the number two offense in football. The 49ers have the number one offense in football. Buffalo dropped back a bit after having to play that really good Minnesota Vikings defense yesterday. So the uh so the 49ers right here have the number one offense in the league. You're trying to keep it that way if you're San Francisco. This is now I can move it to offense only. Pass offenses on the x-axis. They're the best pass offense in the league. So the best pass offense in the league adds a six-time Pro Bowler, a savvy vet. We we know that Brock Purdy and Kyle Shanahan can make these guys work. I think it's just a matter of execution during the last four or five minutes of the game. Of course, there are game moments during the match that lead to this, and we can prepare better.  Every play matters, but if you look at the teams at the top of the standings or the playoffs, I think it's all about execution at the end.  And I believe we have young players who are learning how to do that.  But at the same time, when you can constantly create advantageous positions for yourself in the game, we will achieve our goal.  I sincerely believe this. Yes, I will start.  Listen, Simon, I noticed at practice after Jeff left , you were one of those guys.  You were the one who gathered the team around you before you moved on to individual exercises and prepared for training. To what extent does the departure of such a person make others feel that they need to do more in terms of leadership? I know you've been doing this your whole career, but do you become even more careful when someone like him comes along? Yes, it was a very emotional week for us, losing Jeff, such an important person to our team, a leader that everyone looked up to and who invested so much in us.  So it was definitely a big loss.  So going into practice the next day, I just wanted to make sure the guys had that leadership.  We have great leaders on the team : Jake, Jermaine, John—they are all great leaders.  But I just wanted to take a step forward and say something to the guys to focus everyone on the current moment. Yes, Jeff is gone, but we still have to do our jobs.  We must continue to work.  We must uphold the standard that he set, that we believe in, and we must move on.  And in this league, time doesn't stop.  Time keeps passing. The players continue to get better. The players keep getting worse.  So at that moment I wanted to remind the guys: hey, our careers go on.  Our Titans season continues, we need to be here and now, moving forward and being the best we can be.  And you don't have to be Superman, just do your job at an excellent level and maintain our standard. And how would you say your leadership is about just looking at you, and how much is about speaking up when you feel it's necessary, or is it a combination of both approaches? Yes, I would say it's definitely a combination of both approaches.  You know, especially when you're in a new place, I don't want to be the loudest guy when I join a new team.  I want to prove my worth first.  I want to show everyone that I am consistent in my work.  I am consistent in how I appear on the field.  My work ethic and my habits are the same every day.  I want to demonstrate this to the guys.  And then when they start to see who I am, how I practice, how I act in the locker room, how I act in the quarterbacks' room, you know, I want to speak openly because I've been in this league for a long time.  I've been on really good teams that lost in the Super Bowl.  I've been on teams that didn't make the playoffs and had to deal with adversity and drama all season.  So all my experience in the league—mental, physical, emotional— I want to pass on to other guys and become a leader for them.  But I also want to show the guys that I'm not just talking .  I'm making an effort too.  And even if I'm silent, you can learn just by watching how I work and how I teach every day. Solomon, look at the last few weeks: you guys have created a lot of interceptions, but you've also given up a lot of yards. Are these two things related because you take more risks, or are you just doing one thing well and not the other? You know, I don't think necessarily if you throw more interceptions, you give up more yards.   It's just that sometimes we're not as attentive to detail as we should be.  We allow explosive draws to happen one after another.  And I believe that the main thing we need to stop is these explosive pranks.  But we do a great job with interceptions.  Hook plays simply incredible , giving it his all.  Many guys are taking a step forward and showing very good football.  But we definitely need to keep the yardage under control, you know?  Sometimes we play against players like Joe Burrow, who are the best in the league, they create chances and that's fine, but matches still have to be won.  I think the most important thing in the last few weeks is we've had five or six games where the difference in the score was one possession. These games need to be won in the fourth quarter, and it comes down to details, execution, and the desire to win more than the fear of losing.  And that, I think, is our biggest problem right now.  If we fix this, we can change the whole program, and I believe in the guys in the locker room, I believe in our capabilities, I believe in who we are.  Um, and that's the most important thing—those details, finishing the game and winning in such tight matches, because that's what separates the teams that make the playoffs from the ones that have five and eleven or five and twelve or whatever. Do you feel like you are close to this Certainly.  I feel like we've been close to this all year.  I think there were five or six games where, if we had won, the whole perception of our season would have been completely different.  But this is the NFL.   It does n't matter what could have been, if and if—lost, lost, that's how the season goes.  But I believe we are very close.  We need everyone to believe in our mission, everyone to believe in our path.  It requires attention to the little things: whether it's staying longer after workouts, watching more videos, or taking care of your body.  It is a belief in our entire atmosphere. We're almost there, we're close, but we have to see it through because the league, the fans, the universe don't care that you were close.  You must achieve a result. Solomon, how difficult do you think it will be to overcome that barrier this week against the Jaguars, who are in great offensive form right now? Yes, I know the Jaguars are playing great right now .  First in the division.  Trevor Lawrence is currently showing an incredible level of play.  They have a very good defense and a strong defensive line. So I think every week is the same challenge.  Every week is difficult.  Every week there are new challenges depending on who you're playing against: whether it's the quarterback, the defense, or one of their star players.  But we are very close.  We have to keep believing in the process, keep working and improving every week.  And that's exactly what we do.  So this will be a serious challenge.  Every week is a tough challenge.  We just have to go out, play our best game, act cohesively, believe in each other and get this division win. How do you rate your own game, Solomon ?  I mean the first half of the season, because of course you are familiar with the coaching staff and the system.  How do you feel about how well it suits you? Yes, no, I really like this defense.  I am thrilled with Coach White Cotton.  I like how he lets me play.  I love the intensity and attention to detail that Solomon brings.  Personally, you know, this year I focused on being here and now, not judging myself on every game moment.  This is a new mentality I'm approaching the season with: focusing on the process, not the results.  Yes, I'm not making as many cool game highlights as I would like this year, but I believe it will come if I give it my all every day: coming in early, working, staying after practices, watching game tapes, and doing whatever it takes.  I believe that success will come.  And I play with a level of dedication and intensity that I think is hard to beat. I always run to the ball.  I always try to do the little things right, regardless of whether I made a mistake in the task or not.  I think all this is coming gradually, and I believe they will.  But right now I'm really focused on the process, on being here and now, accepting the outcome, whatever it may be, good or bad, and giving it my all in every moment, trying to be the best version of Solomon Thomas I can be. I believe I can continue to play at a high level every week, I get better with every match and I believe my best games are yet to come. I want to ask about the two guys: what's it like playing with Jacob Martin and how is he doing?  And about Femi, the young player, what do you see in his development? Yes, I really like playing with Jake.  I got to play with him a little bit with the Jets before he was traded.  Jake is a true master of his craft.  He's so good with his hands.  He's like a martial arts master when he uses his hands .  He's a great leader, a great teammate, and just plain fun to play with. It energizes.  We call him a rock star because he lives like a rock star .  His celebration is playing the guitar.  He brings that energy and that life to our defense group.  He inspires others to play the same way, to have fun, to live life to the fullest.  And I think Jake brings incredible intensity and love to the game .  He is very interesting to play with, because he creates more chances for others, attracting the attention of opponents.  He's just a great football player. And then there's Femi, a young guy who impresses me from the very beginning: he does everything consistently, every day—whether it's the sauna, or contrast baths, or training late , or asking questions to the coaches. He is very active and communicates well with everyone.  Femi gives his all in every game.  He constantly appears in the frame on videos.  He always runs to the ball.  He does all the little things right.  Femi will become a big player in this league because of his work;  Even though he is still young, he has the approach of a veteran with eight years of experience.  I am very happy for Femi, proud of him and look forward to his continued growth. Anything else? I can answer one more question, Dwight, if there's anyone else in line.  But I know, Sally, you're focused on your game and helping the team off the field.  I know that every time you move to a new community, you take an active part in its life.  How is life for you here in Nashville How do you try to talk about your foundation and everything related to it? Yes, it really was great.  It's hard in the league to constantly move from one team to another.  This is my fifth team, but in a way it's a blessing, because I can influence the life of a new community.  Nashville has become a great place for me .  There is great food, great people, and a wonderful community. I had the opportunity to visit various schools in the Nashville area, speaking to high school football teams and students about mental health . It was very powerful, especially for me, to see how aware these kids are of mental health issues, what questions they ask when an NFL player comes up to them and talks about something other than football or success. I talk to them about things completely unrelated to sports.  I talk about mental health and they listen, they pay attention, they, uh, ask me questions, they join in the conversation, and that means a lot to me.  And I'm just grateful to have a platform to talk to these kids about what's really important, what we're all going through, especially as young men who may feel pressure to be strong, may feel pressure to pretend that they're okay when they're not, to just have these conversations and say, " Hey, men can cry, men can go through hard times, men are emotional people."  Seeing them listen, having these conversations, seeing it in their eyes and in their reactions—it was really nice, I'm grateful for this opportunity here in Nashville, and I'm looking forward to continuing. Chris, tell me. And one more quick question: did you mention, uh, filling the void or, I guess, the vocal void that was left after Jeff.  You watched the two games he played for the Bears, and what did you think of it Oh, of course, you know, we love Jeff .  Jeff very quickly became a close friend to all of us on the team, to our entire defensive line.  Just the way he communicates with each of us.  So we support him, and we do so sincerely.  We want to see him succeed, and he's doing great.  You know, two seiki for two games .  You see his intensity on the field, how he lights up.  It's nice to see, and it still motivates us, even though he's not with us, just watching him play.  We tell ourselves: we want to continue to hold this bar for his sake.  And we love Jeff, we're glad he's doing well, and we're glad he's winning games.  He deserves it.
