You know, you get your gold jacket eventually and it does make us happy to see that this new ownership, this new staff here >> has true value in the past and what was the Redskins in this burgundy and gold. >> They won the Super Bowl in 1982, right? >> That was 44 years ago, right? >> 44 >> That's his number. >> But it shouldn't take 44 years to honor someone of that caliber. >> Yeah, without a doubt. >> You know, so I just let you know what this new ownership group is coming in and they right in a lot of wrongs that they've seen. And it it's been multiple ownerships here. But Riggo was a guy I think that thing should have happened a long time ago. You know, point-blank. He's a Hall of Famer. >> He's a Ring of Famer. >> Why was his number still sitting there? >> That's crazy. >> That's just the way I look at it. >> Yeah, I mean I I don't see many people clamoring to wear 44 in this generation. >> don't. >> So they could have put that thing up there a long time ago. >> Well, nobody wore it, but they hadn't officially said it was retired. >> Because this is the the the guys Booga, uh Jaybird, those were the the guys that handled the equipment. >> Mhm. >> You wouldn't get that >> mention that 44. >> what I'm saying? 44 [laughter] was retired in the hearts of everyone. It just wasn't officially done. And Josh and his group came in and officially got that done. >> And it's just important again because Rigo was able to enjoy every bit of this. I have no doubt that this had a lot to do with him helping us in preseason as well. Great to see Rigo get that love. And even better to see Dan Quinn out at the podium. Let's hear from our head coach. >> All right, let's get rolling. Um frustrating game. And once again, like we have not nailed our complimentary football. And I'll keep saying it until we do. Um we're halfway through the season and that all has to click. Um after stops, don't think we capitalized. Um two takeaways. I think we only got three points out of it. We had some opportunities for fourth-down stops defensively to get those stops to get it flipped the other way. So all that said, it's a short week um against our division leader on the road. And we got to go. And we have to play all three phases together. Um seen too much of it where it's part of it, not the whole thing. And so that's what we're going to continue to just practice it and that has to get right. It just has to. Too far along to not have it all working together. All right, let's get rolling. >> Dan, offense got off to a pretty good start and then seemed to >> Can you start I missed the first part. >> Yeah, sorry. Um the offense got off to a pretty good start but seemed to fall a little flat there. What what was sort of missing? >> Yeah, I I did like the way that we started too, Nikki. I felt that way. Um to see us, you know, have some runs at action to go and I didn't feel like we were able to sustain that. And you know, like to get ahead and then here's a chance even to like you know, get a takeaway and go further to go. Um but like my biggest example is like even the complimentary we had a chance to be on our 2-minute to go. Um we got a takeaway. I think it was um maybe a fumble recovery. And then we turned it over again. They get a field goal. So looking back to it, you know, like I'll give them credit too. Like I want to watch the tape like from a front standpoint. But I liked how we started but like just to not see that sustained, Nikki. That's the thing that's uh you know, make makes like especially frustrating. >> And then in the third quarter of the decision to challenge the way um that Amik was involved in. What what went into that? What was sort of the thinking there? >> The one that was overturned? >> Ultimately upheld. Not reversed. >> Yeah. Um I think just they said the second the first catch was the bobble that we're saying and then the second step maybe with them was established. So we're thinking all right, the first one the second one was you know, like showing completion of the catch. And so after review they thought maybe it was bobbled on the first step. So then that didn't make it into the the second step meaning that became the first. But I think on those ones sometimes like you take a shot too, you know, when it's a one that you think is reasonable to go. When it's clear and obvious many times that gets replay assisted. But in that moment I felt like this was one if it's close roll the dice. I didn't think it was um I wouldn't have done it at about I think it was no shot at it. >> Uh Dan on that uh final play what went into the decision to go with the lateral play instead of maybe taking a shot at the directly at the end zone. >> Yeah, so there's two plays that you come in and so on the first one um you're you know, like taking a shot to the end zone just like you described and uh sometimes the check for that against the team that does like a what we call like a zero blitz or a max blitz, you want to okay, you're the other play where you can't block them all up and so they did good job disguising showing that one. So, we got to the second play of what would been like everybody blitzing, check it down and move forward from there. So, with 8 seconds left you want two chances at something and so to not have those you know, like didn't love the our execution at the our end. >> And then on the injury front, you had a couple guys go down and and Lucas Patrick and Amik Robertson. Do you have any sort of >> The only one I do have is that with Lucas not coming back, he's in the concussion protocol, but I'll give you some updates tomorrow whenever we talk next regarding anyone else. That's the only one that the medical team hit me on prior to tonight. >> Um Dan, there were a couple players who were talking about how like they knew what the Rams offense were going to do to O'Connell getting the ball to Puka. You know that. How hard was it Why was it so hard I guess to stop especially that like Puka where you know he's very good, but >> Yeah, yeah, for sure. And I'll give him credit, too. So, the inside style of runs I guess what they've been, you know, demonstrating of like the run game and inside and I knew that was going to be one of the strengths of their team. I thought both the backs had showed, you know, good production doing that. With Nacua there I knew there'd also been some on the screen side of things. So, it's not all drop backs to go and I think that's part of what makes him unique is his catch and run, you know, ability where it's not just downfield throws. So, on those you have to be able to roll up and tackle well, John, too. Like he may get X number of catches for not too far down the field, but knowing that like hey man, you got to go get your tackle due. So, having too many yards that that's that was big for me. >> And there's still nine games left, but do you feel like you're running out of time here in terms of around >> Yeah, I think it speaks to the importance of our division leader, you know, right away. And so, um it's difficult locker room like we got to turn the page quickly, you know, to get to that because um we talked earlier okay, this is where we are, but like we also know like men, like this we have to play at our best. >> With Golden, uh, how difficult a spot is that? >> Go in, how well has he practiced to earn the backup spot? And is Allegretti out of the picture at center? >> Um, we've went with how we've been practicing more like Nick at guard, and so both of those and Matt there. So, in that moment I would have felt comfortable with Nick as well, but I thought let's give the guys got the most reps of where we've been hitting and putting Nick at guard. So, that was kind of not kind of that was the decision behind it. It's difficult, but um, like he's also like this is, you know, part of the gig. >> Uh, Dan, on the offensive line, Brandon had a couple of penalties again. I just wonder like what's the in the heat of the game, you know, I know you don't want to make changes just for change's sake, but at what point do you say, "Hey, we got to get somebody else in there that if if he's struggling?" >> Yes. And uh, I want to go back to look, we've uh, we put a lot of work um, daily to like what could change to get some of these false starts off. So, to have still two remain, I think Sam's might have been a holding right on the one that was prior to the um, turnover. So, like to look, um, we've we've made adjustments on how many cadences, what types and that. So, I just want to see if it's a product of uh, too much anticipation against a good rusher. And that's different to me than like a lack of focus. That makes sense, Dave. So, I I want to I want I'll give you a better answer once I have a chance to look at them. >> And just I just want to be clear on Allegretti. He's healthy, there's nothing >> Yes. Yeah. Yeah, we've just been working him more guard and Matt at center. And you know, if we have to change, we'll see what next week looks like as well. >> Coach, going back to the last two plays there from the 32. You'd mentioned you didn't like the execution. Can you get more into Was that just called that play for Chayce or is that read out based on the blitz? >> Um, yeah, it has to be like one that you get to a second play. And um, you know, like it's the right, you know, adjustment to make it going. So, how long do you wait? Do you get the full protection and, you know, try to throw a Hail Mary because it's hard to on a Hail Mary get everybody scrambling and buy time when they're bringing everyone. So, that's the juxtapose of like get to a max protection, buy time, or that's another alternative play. So, um the one before, it was really the one I wanted to see more execution when there was maybe 8 seconds. At that point, you know, there's just two plays remaining in the game and you want to give yourself a chance. >> Is that call cuz they kept three across the goal line on the previous play and you're expecting that again? >> Um I think it's more like take his three two of what, you know, could be and what they've done and so I'm like also like I want to give them I'm not looking to, you know, take away them, but I just want to see us like give us a real shot at it. So. >> Dan, you guys um obviously shorthanded at receiver. Look like Stefon Diggs wasn't playing a ton the first half cuz you guys were going with like 12 and 13 personnel a lot. Was that part of the plan? >> Um no. No, it wasn't any um like further design than another. Um we've actually done less multiples of who and what, especially um when we were, you know, lighter at than we have been. So, um but no, there was no design of having less, just how we're going to feature a certain play. >> And for Van Jefferson to go from not being on the roster to no catches to kind of leading you guys, especially in the first half, how much was that anticipated going in? Wouldn't say it was anticipated um then, but I would say like this is somebody that uh is a respected player around here and um I can remember after camp having a hard conversation and him coming back on a practice squad when we had a very healthy wide receiver room, knowing it would take a leap of faith to still come knowing that there were, you know, six players already on the active and so putting the trust into it, to put the work in, um and here he is getting a chance. And so, like to score early and, you know, like came back, you know, getting banged up and made another catch later. >> Dan, we obviously see how things ended, but the beginning of the game, Stafford, I think through the first quarter, only had about 33 passing yards. They didn't convert a third down through the first nine tries. What went well, do you think, in the beginning and obviously what kind of shifted? >> Yeah, I was pleased. Um I was pleased overall on third down to be honest with you. Um I'd like to go back and look to see the fourth downs of why. I've seen you know, us play with, you know, good discipline on a lot of the third downs and they put a lot of work into that. And so, there at sometimes it can be easier to go to one person, one location. Um but the long one at the end, I think it was a you know, like big conversion in the fourth. That was the one man would certainly like to have back. So, um they're gaining um on some things. I like that we got the ball again. And so, that might be, you know, five or six games, you know, in a row. So, I'm feeling some of that. It was good to see um that take place and we'll need more of that for sure. >> Take three more? >> Hey Don, just how would you evaluate the offensive line's performance today? >> You know, I'd rather give you a better answer tomorrow. You know, like just there's a lot to to go in and consider and see what matchups did we chip, where did we help, you know, what was in the run game, why did some go early and some not. So, um I'd like to you know, I don't want to just cast out and say where I think it is, but I'll I'll certainly look at it tonight. Um and watch it and then, like I said, we'll make any adjustments that we need to um as we head into tomorrow cuz you know, in 72 hours back on the plane and like go get ready again. >> Don, obviously Myles Garrett's a really accomplished player, but what did you think of his performance first game back from the injury? >> Yeah, I'm I was expecting him to play well. Like that's usually what you see with him. Um he's got unique get off, JP, and uh leverage to go. So, he looked like a guy who hadn't been out. Um that's what I saw. So, like I said, I want to look at our tape and see where they go and how they deployed him, but not surprised um to see him perform well. That's we see that pretty regularly. >> Listening to you and and talking to the players last week, it was obvious that stopping Nick Bosa was such a a major focal point for the defense. Was there anything else you can do with a guy like >> You can and uh And I I do like their screen package. Sean's had a good one running backs, tight ends. They tried the tight end one, the running backs to go. So, um there'll be some that we'll want back um when we call like cloud to a certain player. Um man-to-mans, it's harder unless you're doubling someone. But, um in the zones, um it can be challenging due to Matthew's ability to deliver the ball to the right location. And so, that can be true in zone where like if quarterback knows right where to go, that's hard. But, um still 150 is still 150. >> Liam, last one. >> Coach, on that fourth down about midway through the fourth quarter where you ended up taking a delay of game, did you guys have a play called there or was that >> Gosh. >> Sorry. Thanks. >> You're welcome. >> All right. Thanks, coach. >> All right. Thank you. >> James is coming right in. >> That was our head coach, Dan Quinn. And we are going to keep it right here cuz we are expecting Jayden Daniels at the podium. 80 seconds. >> Jayden, we know you don't like losing. How frustrating are these close but not enough games? >> Um yeah, frustrating is is is >> You got off to a good start there, but what sort of wasn't working or kind of fell flat there with the offense? we just whole unit didn't execute. And regardless like, you know, for our second down and credit to them, like um when we got into our third down, they got into their packages that uh that were really just go out there and let these all-pros and you know, all the famous rush and stuff like that. And uh and back and they knew the ball had to come out quick. So, we just didn't execute any of the play calls that were that were called um as a as a whole unit. >> On that final drive, the incomplete to Antonio Williams, it looked like there may have been a miscommunication there. Do you Do you recall what happened Yeah, I mean, it's just a miscommunication between both of us. >> Jade, on that final play, Dan Quinn said it was a check, I guess, that you guys could either throw it in the end zone or throw it underneath. What did you see pre-snap that made you go with the underneath option? >> Um I mean, going up to the watching the film like, you know, I think that had one versus uh I want to say the Raiders, I want to I want to say. I'm not not too sure. Don't call me on that, but they bring pressure on that, you know, in those moments. Um last play game, I think it was like 7-8 seconds left on the play clock. Uh they want to get the ball out the the quarterback's hand as fast as possible, so um you know, you could know you have to take a shot to the end zone, so if they could get home before you get the ball up or you let your guys get down there. Um you know, that's probably ideal, so uh that was the play call that was that was called, and we had to execute it. >> Jade, on that final play, it looked like they were looking like they were going to send some heat, but they ended up only sending five, I think, on that on the one that you threw underneath to Okonkwo. Was that a situation where you couldn't like adjust to throw it into the end zone? Did you have to stick with the lateral play at that point? >> It was a play call, we got to execute >> Jade, what happened on that fumble? >> Um I mean, I got to have I tried to step up, and I seen I want to say Van on the corner. I was trying to throw it in, uh Myles Garrett happened. >> Do you feel like you guys are starting to run out of time here to really kind of get back in this thing? I think like next week is must win. >> Jade, uh how would you evaluate the offensive line before offensive line's performance in front of you today? >> Um yeah, I think it is they they battled, right? Um you know, it's tough, and you know, you're asking a lot of people to to, you know, hold up and and block uh obviously Aaron Donald, Myles Garrett, um and it's tough, but we got to be able to go out there and communicate and and pass things off. Um, and just hold up uh as much as we can, but uh you know, you can't really stop a lot of people, but you can slow them down, right? >> And then what do you think you can do to get the run game going a little better? >> Um, I think it's just the the play calls. Um, we got to be able to to execute, you know, hit our landmarks uh within the offense and go from there. >> Jayden, how how difficult a spot is it for Matt to come in midway through a game against that front? >> Um, I mean, if I was Matt, it would be very difficult. So, uh I would assume it's it's super difficult at that moment. You come out of halftime, um you know, your first game that you're ever playing and you got to go out there and block that front. >> Jayden, the end of this game seemed felt at least from my perspective similar to the end of the San Francisco game. And what is it besides just, you know, saying execute that is preventing you guys in those moments from executing? So, I don't know I mean, I think at that point in time you just like execute. I don't know what to really say about that. Like, you just, you know, we get in those moments and we got to finish. Like, we got to make plays and that's from myself, that's from O-line, the running backs, receivers. Um, you know, the play calls and stuff like that. Like, we we got to make plays. Like, regardless what they call, like, we got to make plays. >> Jayden, what um from your perspective, what went right on the screen pass to uh Rashad in the first quarter? >> Uh, we caught them in a in a double cat pressure. Um, you know, just based off our formation, our alignment, uh they blitzed both both the corners and we caught them at the right time. So, that's what went well, and they got the ball in Rashad's hand and he did the rest. >> Jayden, on that fourth down you guys had that delay of game. DK said you guys had a play called. So, what prevented you guys maybe able to get that off on time? Was it the Rams front? Was it the play call? Was it having a new center? >> Um cover zero. They're about to bring um just a pressure. Trying to communicate, get the ball in my hand. Uh and you know, we just didn't uh when I was clapping for the ball, we didn't we just didn't snap it. So, uh yeah, we didn't get the ball. It's it's on us as players. >> And on the last play of the game, it looked like as soon as you threw it, you were booking it down the field. Is that something where it's a designed lateral to you or is that just you trying to stay alive? >> no, it's just stay alive. I mean, uh you know, chase the ball. Yeah, in that situation, uh you know, Jalen made made a play, made a guy miss, and I'm just trying to chase the ball just in case, you know, a lot of people come around and he's able to lateral to me, we can kind of play that game from there. >> You guys are halfway through the season, and the pre-snap penalties and the false starts, those kind of things continue to to bite you. I know you guys have tried a bunch of different stuff, but what can you do at this point, and and how do you get that turned around with, you know, eight, nine games remaining? >> Um my thing is just a It's just a focus thing. It's focus. Like where like we can't sometimes we can't communicate, you know, perfectly. Uh regardless of like I have to go out there and check something or call something like, you know, we're we're dealing versus a play clock also and and it's just a it's a loss of of focus. Like that's that's the main thing. Like we just got to mentally be in tune each and every play, reset, refocus, uh so we can go out there and be the best that we can. >> Jaylen, kind of building off of that, actually. Um what do you kind of do to make sure that your cadence is as consistent as possible? >> Um I mean, I I I go to feedback like they have they have to I go to O-line and they tell me um you know, can you be louder and you know, stuff like that. Um most definitely that's something that I have to adjust, but uh for the most part, you know, I'm just trying to give them mental cues of like, you know, we're about to go like, you know, I'm about to call for the snap and stuff like that. Um but I try to be consistent, you know, we we kind of they need me to go up there and voice record or keep going through that. Like, you know, I'm willing to do whatever, but we got to get this cleaned up. >> Now, the injuries are part of the game, but as you go through and you have to introduce new weapons, like today was Van Jefferson, how do you make sure that mentally you're not getting tighter with the football as you bring more guys up? >> Um, I mean, just dealing with the card the cards I was dealt. Um, you know, playing the hand, so I got to go out there with those guys. I got to trust those guys to make plays and like you said, Van made some plays. Uh, Jahan Dotson made a big catch at the end of the game, so just trusting those guys and I see the work that they put in and what they've done from OTAs all the way up to this point, so uh, I trust them to go out there and make plays. Thank you all. >> That was our quarterback Jayden Daniels. Now, it is time for our postgame delivery brought to you by Paisano's, the official pizza of Washington Commanders. Order now at paisanospizza.com. Pizza, wings, and of course, Commanders football. Fellas, as we close out the show today, you look at that road ahead, short week for us, but a beatable team in the New York Giants. >> Yeah, you got it. And it's about pride, man. You know, you you you you got to figure out a way to get this thing going. We've talked a lot about they've talked a lot about what they know they can do. Hell, go out there and get it done. >> Yeah, sooner or later they have to work. And I think one of the things about, you know, the situation we're in now, I told you, we've been here before. I've been on teams where we were 3 and 6 and went out there and ran the table. So, these guys understand that they want to play football, you go out here and take advantage of these games in front of you. >> Without a doubt, still a lot of football to be played and remember we will have content for you all week long on the Commanders YouTube page and the Commanders social. I'm your host Brian Custer Jr. We'll see y'all on primetime Thursday night football. >> I'm going to get some primetime.

text: We use the term must-win a lot. I think now after that loss on Sunday, we're going to be talking more and more about a must-win Thursday and beyond. Anthony, >> you know, some folk hell, some folks going to be talking about the draft here before long. But look, I wins are always good. I like to see wins, but when we going to run this intro is right now. >> Hail [music] to the commanders. It's the Commander Squad. Everything Washington Commanders every week covering all the big hits and gamechanging plays from [music] the heart of the nation's capital. The way only the Locked on Podcast Network can rally the Burgundy and Gold. The Commander [music] Squad Show starts now. And we start with Anthony Armstrong and Nick Ashu. David Harrison going to join us in a few minutes. We're all on the road. We're all all over the place. And this is why we put it on the calendar, Anthony. That's why we've got to do this. Uh I would love to put a game that is a win on the calendar for the Commanders. That did not happen against the Rams. It's going to need to happen against the Giants. We're going to look a little bit ahead to the Giants game at the end of the show. Of course, more of that is going to come right before the game, which is a short week this week. It's a Thursday night game. Uh I will say this though, Anthony, the least surprising thing that we had on Sunday was that Miles Garrett was a badass and Miles Garrett plowed through the Commander offensive line. And you know what? Here's the thing. I'm not blaming Jaden. I'm not blaming even the offensive linemen that weren't very good out there because you know what? Miles Garrett is so damn good. Nobody should be surprised that he came back looking like an absolute monster for the Rams. >> Man, look, that that sucker came out there 25 snaps like a little cup of coffee. Man, he didn't miss a beat. And honestly, that that was like one part that I didn't really plan for. I you know, I had my keys that said, um, what up D Harrison? Look at y'all got the green. >> Harrison jumping on now with us from the car. What's up, buddy? >> Yeah, y'all got the green memo. I'm about to go change. Um, no. See, the thing is like when you get when you had Miles come in there, um, like it it just throws off your numbers, right? You're already going to give the respect and and you know, pay attention to Aaron Donald. You're going to you're going to give him, you know, what's due and he's enough of a challenge. And this is a four down, you know, rushing team, right? So, here's how it all kind of builds out. Then they were finding way well they're four down rushing team. Now you have Miles Garrett. So now you have to give extra eyes to him. You have a secondary that they can sit back and they can chill a little bit more but they were putting him in situation where it was just one-on-one. I mean him standing up doing the ISO uh Euro step against your rookie against really against anybody, right? I don't know any lineman. Like this is the only thing that you could do in this situation is like see if you can shift your lineman and be like, "Hey, can you can like Trent Williams move to center because Miles Garrett's right there, but he can also then move back on the outside." So like it's it's one of them unfortunate like matchup things. You you can plan for it coming into the week. I'm pretty sure they didn't like have, you know, Jonathan Joseph's doing Miles Garrett stuff in the middle of the field trying to trying to prepare for that. Dude, the beast like chalk went up. He had all the Infinity Stones. Like, well, I don't know what to [laughter] tell you, man. Like, that's it. He's just he's just that damn good. And, you know, just got you just got to take your L's, man. Just got to say, you know what? Those are some stories I'll say as a as a as a rookie. Matt Goldman, you know what? what you welcome to the NFL moment when I looked up and Miles Garrett was doing the crossover like that right there is a one-of-a-kind moment. Eyes are probably big as hell. Um anyways, David, take it away. >> Man, I mean that's a tough draw, right? That's a tough draw. I've talked to a lot of linemen over the years about kind of some of their toughest draws and Miles Garrett is is definitely a name that that comes up for the guys who have had to try uh to block him. And I say try to block him because nobody can do that, you know, by themselves. And look, you know, as much as we all want to see the commanders like double team Miles Garrett every single snap and and all these, like it's just sometimes it's not feasible to just all the time commit two guys, you know, to one guy and and do those types of things. And sometimes, man, you just got to be able to try to live uh as much as you can. And, you know, Miles this this this go around, he got the better of the Washington Commanders. I've also seen it where he came in with the Cleveland Browns and, you know, the Washington Mayers were able to do enough and sometimes they chipped them. Sometimes they do him, sometimes they left him one-on-one, but they were able to do enough that Miles didn't really have a great impact on the game. So, it kind of goes both ways and and you know, that's just kind of how it goes sometimes. Just like, let me give a shout out my guy Michael Bonitz Dolvin. This is the hat that he wore into the ring this this this last week, his pro debut. Signed that bad boy for me. Look at that autograph. >> Autograph in his pro boxing debut. So, I had to give a little shout out to my guy there. But yeah, man. Look, that's that's a tough draw no matter how you slice it. Uh Matt Goldin, you know, uh took it like a pro as best you could in the locker room, stood there like a man and got asked the tough questions and gave some really good answers and owned it and you could tell that, you know, he wasn't happy about it and and no competitor is going to go out there and say, "Ah, it's Miles Garrett." Ah, that's okay. No, no. Matt, Matt wasn't happy either. But he's going to grow from it, man. He's going to grow from it and someday hopefully it's going to make him better. You know, having a block Miles Garrett is sort of like being at the plate when you've got a closer that can throw 102 mph fast and that's all they throw and you know it's coming and you still can't hit it. Like sometimes it's just you kind of have to look at it and I think David, you kind of put it the best way. It's like you kind of just look at it as a welcome to the NFL moment. But even like veteran offensive linemen that are really good get beat like a drum by Miles Garrett. I mean there's a reason why.
